With the technology of 0.18 μm GaAs pHEMT technology, this LNA yields low noise as well as high gain with very low power consumption based on a self-bias architecture. The self-bias structure simplifies power management as it utilizes a single supply. The design inductively degenerates sources to improve broadband matching in addition to noise performance, thereby reducing size and complexity needed in matching networks for the wideband operations. From the simulations carried out on ADS, stability was ensured, using stability coefficients and realizing optimized input/output impedances in Smith chart tuning. The LNA achieves minimum noise figure, with a small-signal gain more than 10 dB and p1dB more than 12 dBm which show good linearity as well.

articleTitle: Enhanced Wildfire Detection in Forest Areas via OPENCV with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Smoke and Flame Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Forest fire detection is a critical component of environmental management systems, enabling early identification and response to mitigate devastating impacts on ecosystems, infrastructure, and human lives. A system utilizing OpenCV-based algorithms for real-time detection of forest fires. By employing HSV color space for segmentation and deep learning techniques, the proposed system achieves robust identification of fire regions. The Fmeasures are used to assess performance, showing its effectiveness. Enhancing such systems can significantly reduce fire- related losses globally. In difficult situations like dense smoke or at night, integrating multi-sensor data fusion—for example, merging satellite and thermal imaging data—can improve detection accuracy even more. Furthermore, by integrating real-time alarm systems with GIS mapping, authorities may more effectively deploy resources and pinpoint fire breakouts, cutting down on reaction times and minimizing fire-related losses worldwide.

articleTitle: AI Driven Rat Detection for Warehouse
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The project’s goal is to create a system for controlling insect activity and monitoring of warehouses in sizable grain storage facilities. The idea behind the system uses neural networks, deep learning algorithms, and imagery processing methods to identify, monitor, track, and notify users of the activity of pests, notably rats, in real-time. By using algorithms that use deep learning for real-time object recognition and authentication, rats may be accurately identified. In addition, the sensors augment optical detection by using non-visual methods to detect motion and activity, providing full surveillance regardless of regions that are completely concealed. The system’s network of carefully positioned imaging devices and sensors allows for constant, continuous surveillance of the warehouse ambiance. The system activates and displays an indication once it recognises a rat, and it logs the precise time and place of the event. To ensure prompt action and response, warehouse administrators get updates in real time via email, SMS, or a mobile app. Through the application of artificial intelligence (AI), this initiative seeks to improve the security of food, reduce monetary damage, and revolutionize pest control at storage facilities for grain.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Open-Set Seed Classification Using Hyperspectral and RGB Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The classification of seed varieties is important to maintain the productivity of agriculture and check fraudulence and the control of quality in seed businesses. The earlier approaches for the seed classification conventional techniques are tedious and rudimentary, besides being to an extent, arbitrary and though permissible they have low scalability, especially to big data or even as real-time solutions. This paper is a suggestion of using hybrid deep learning framework open to hyperspectral imaging with HSI and RGB Imaging. To this end, the newly proposed Dual Deep Support Vector Data Description model and a vision transformer-based architecture are used for our classification task of known seed types along with the rejection of unknown seeds. The framework uses incremental learning techniques, and spatial-spectral features as well as attention-based bands to enhance the scalability of the technique and its performance. Comparing the results of the present work with previous techniques, it can be concluded that the proposed methods of hybrid imaging and improved deep learning model may help to solve the problems of classic, as well as open-set recognition in agriculture. Future studies could apply this approach to other crops with the goal to pursue precision agriculture and improve world’s food safety.

articleTitle: Decoding Digital Intruders: Machine Learning Strategies for Botnet Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The word "Robot-Network" is where the term "Botnet" originates. Botnets can harm our devices by creating damage or posing hazards to the computer in the form of viruses, malware, spyware, and other malicious software. Malware is becoming more and more prevalent every day. There is a big concern from malicious apps that transform mobile devices to bots that could be a part of a larger botnet. It is important to detect mobile botnets to keep our devices safe from hackers. The most popular mobile operating system, Android, is rapidly being targeted by malware. Machine learning techniques are implemented to identify botnets in a variety of ways. We describe a Machine Learning based strategy to detect mobile botnets in this study. Low FP (false positive) rates and real identification rates are few goals of the suggested method. Additionally, utilizing the same dataset and multiple machine learning methods, the objective is to enhance identification accuracy. Using various ways to get the best output and accuracy, as well as classifying botnets into families, will help to keep our devices safe from botnets.

Author Keywords: ABIS (Android Botnet Identification System) and Malware

articleTitle: Hybrid Heuristic Optimization of Deep Learning Models for Robust Plant Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Plant diseases directly affect farm output by lowering grain, fruit, and vegetable quality, threatening global food security. Thus, farmers inspect plant leaves with their eyes. Plant leaf monitoring is unreliable and error-prone. A multitude of deep learning algorithms have been developed to detect plant leaf diseases; however, most rely on low-resolution photos utilizing convolutional neural nets (CNNs). This research seeks to create an improved nine-layer the CNN network model for the accurate classification of leaf-related illnesses. A contrast enhancement approach is used to pre-process plant leaf pictures. Following binary thresholding, the pre-processed pictures are separated into leaf images and abnormality segmented using the "Enhanced U-Net (EU-Net)" approach. A Multilevel Feature Fusion Network Convolutional Neural Network (MFFN-CNN) is employed to categorize illnesses of leaves based on segmented images. The "Hybrid Leader Cat Swarm Optimization(HLCSO)" method improves U-Net parameter optimization. The effectiveness of the leaf diagnostic model is demonstrated experimentally employing a variety of factors through the use of numerous baseline approaches.

articleTitle: Co-ordinate Measurement Machine Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Over the past 20 years, contactless measuring system application has grown significantly, especially in the area of coordinate measurement. The growing use of these systems in industry has increased interest in determining their correctness, particularly in research facilities. Fiducial markers are a promising development in contactless measurements, especially in dimensional metrology. In order to obtain accurate detection and measurement of the distance between circular objects, this research provides a sophisticated coordinate measuring system that uses ArUco markers and OpenCV. In order to ensure accurate measurements, it is imperative that the ArUco markers are used to confirm that objects are positioned correctly within the Region of Interest (ROI) and to maintain a constant distance. After this preliminary check, the system incorporates an Excel interface that is easy to use, enabling users to choose circles by hand using their x and y coordinates. Users can choose which circles to measure by selecting ’y’ for yes or ’n’ for no. The system will then determine the distance between the circles automatically. By combining the accuracy of automatic detection with the adaptability of manual selection, this method creates a measurement process that is both highly precise and flexible. The system’s usefulness for applications requiring precise spatial measurements across multiple sectors has been proven by comparing its performance with conventional manual approaches.

articleTitle: Transforming Agriculture: Deep Learning for Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The largest agricultural country, India, derives quite a good portion of its economy from agriculture. Leaf diseases are manifested by severe yield losses whereby farmers’ lives and the main food security of the nation as a whole might be negatively affected. The Indian environment which is distinct for its diversity of climatic region and vegetation is vulnerable to almost all possible leaf diseases. Thus, there is a need for thorough research and surveillance on plant health. In the face of the rising worldwide attention on sustainable use and food production, appropriate management strategies are crucial to decrease chemical pesticide usage and its environmental impact, by using the high-level Deep Learning (DL) methods to make predictions as well as to identify the leaf diseases. Additionally, mobile technology would offer a scalable way to achieve cost-effective monitoring, thus allowing for more productive and environmentally friendly agriculture throughout various Indian regions. To strengthen agriculture, a CNN-based DL model (CNN_LR) is proposed to enhance leaf disease detection for achieving 96.35% accuracy in agriculture.

articleTitle: Document Query Response Using Microsoft-Phi-3-Mini-4K
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The role of automated mechanisms such as chatbots has improved in today’s environment of rapid technological progress which is majorly attributed to the growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based solutions. The ability of such systems to interact with questions concerning PDFs can completely transform support and after sales services in the automotive field where time and resources can be saved. Within this context, this work analyses the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the development of RAG based applications to create a smarter and confidentiality-driven chatbot to preserve the privacy of individuals and companies alike.

articleTitle: A Study on Intelligibility, Naturalness and Fluency of Text-to-Speech Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Text-to-Speech (TTS) technology advancements have resulted in the developing of sophisticated models like Tacotron and WaveNet. This research evaluates these models based on clarity, naturalness, and flow. Tacotron employs a comprehensive architecture that converts text into mel-spectrograms, excelling in prosody and fluency. WaveNet, a probabilistic model, directly generates raw audio waveforms, delivering exceptional sound quality. The LJSpeech dataset assessed performance through metrics such as Word Error Rate (WER) and Mean Opinion Score (MOS). Tacotron achieved a WER of 6.2%, indicating strong fluency with some alignment challenges. WaveNet outperformed Tacotron with a WER of 4.7% and a MOS of 4.6, demonstrating greater naturalness but some minor fluency issues. Tacotron is ideal for expressive applications, while WaveNet excels in realism. Future research could explore hybrid models to combine these strengths and address current limitations..

articleTitle: Road Pothole Detection and Reporting System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Road pothole detection and management can be made easier with the innovative Automated Pothole Detection and Reporting System. By automatically identifying potholes and documenting their locations using mobile devices and advanced data gathering techniques, the technology lessens the need for manual inspections. The gathered data is stored in a centralized database to guarantee that all of the information is compiled and easily accessible for analysis. With an accuracy of 87.67%, the technology offers dependable detection that facilitates effective planning for road repair.Pothole reports may be effectively managed and visualized by municipal authorities through the system’s user-friendly admin interface, which enhances monitoring and repair priorities. Road safety and vehicle damage are improved and responses are made faster and more precise thanks to the system’s optimization of the detection, reporting, and repair processes. Additionally, data-driven insights make it possible to allocate maintenance resources more effectively and guarantee that pothole repairs are prioritized according to their location and severity. This initiative uses technology to improve road safety and streamline maintenance procedures, which is a significant improvement in urban infrastructure management.

articleTitle: Transfer and Bayesian Learning Approaches for Land Use and Land Cover Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) classification is essential for understanding the impact of both human activities and natural processes on the Earth’s surface. This classification plays a critical role in deforestation, urban planning, and damage assessment. However, traditional machine learning techniques often face challenges in achieving consistent accuracy in diverse datasets. In this study, we implement transfer learning and Bayesian learning approaches to enhance the accuracy and robustness of LULC classification. Transfer learning leverages knowledge from previous classification problems, while Bayesian learning addresses uncertainties in the classification process. Using the Remote Sensing Image Classification Benchmark (RSI-CB128) dataset, the study evaluates the performance of Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Mobile Neural Networks (MobileNet), Inception Neural Networks (InceptionNet), Densely Connected Convolutional Networks (DenseNet) and Efficient Neural Networks (EfficientNet). The study also investigates the impact of varying the Bayesian layers on model performance, finding that a medium number of layers optimally captures model uncertainty. The results indicate that the transfer learning models, particularly MobileNet, achieved the highest accuracy of 97. 48% compared to 90. 33% for Bayesian CNN. These findings suggest that transfer learning techniques are highly effective for LULC classification, providing a reliable method for practical applications in remote sensing.

Author Keywords: land use and land cover classification

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for EMG Signal Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: We present a comparative analysis of different machine learning algorithms for classifying electromyography (EMG) signals for the application of prosthetic arm development. We applied four machine learning algorithms, namely Support Vector Machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Trees, and Logistic Regression. These algorithms classified the signals into three classes mentioned. Our results show that SVM achieved the highest accuracy at 83 %, followed by KNN (77 %), Logistic Regression (75 %), and Decision Tree (74 %). These findings suggest that SVM is the most promising approach for EMG signal multiclass classification for the mentioned application. While these results provide a solid foundation, we discuss potential improvements through hyperparameter tuning and study with real EMG sensor data for prosthetics movement. This study contributes to the development of more responsive and intuitive machine learning-powered prosthetic arms, potentially enhancing the quality of life for individuals with upper limb amputations.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification in MRI Scans Using Shape Features & Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: A brain tumor is an unusual growth of cells in the brain that can be either cancerous or non-cancerous. These tumors are the most common malignant primary brain tumors of the central nervous system. They can affect brain function by putting pressure on nearby nerves, blood vessels, and tissues. Accurate early diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment. MRI is commonly used to detect and classify brain tumors as malignant or benign. In this process, MRI images from the Figshare dataset are used, to segment these tumors using various processing techniques. Shape features are extracted for classification, and then various machine learning algorithms are used which perform both classification and regression. These features are fed to these algorithms such as ANN, SVM, and Random Forest.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Advanced GAN Architectures for Robust Image Dehazing in Synthetic and Real-World Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: One typical phenomenon that impairs or lessens visibility is haze. It creates several issues for applications like security surveillance, autonomous cars, satellite imagery where high resolution captures are necessary. Therefore, clearing up haze from the imagery of scenes is an urgent need for good vision. Different kinds of Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) are being used in addition to traditional dehazing processes recently to reduce noise and enhance dehazing performance. However, it's unclear how well these algorithms would work with hazy photos taken "in the wild" and how we might assess the state of the art. To close this gap, a thorough comparison of two cutting-edge models— GAN and Wasserstein GAN, that dehaze a single image is presented. Testing was done using a benchmark dataset that included both synthetic and real-world hazy photos. The resulting outcomes are assessed numerically and qualitatively. Among these strategies, the WGAN performs the best.

articleTitle: Tiered gPTP: A Simulative Study on Balancing Time-Sync Accuracy and Coverage with Time Source Replication
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Deterministic Networking (DetNet) is designed for real-time applications in wide-area networks requiring time synchronization within 1 μs. However, gPTP has the problem of decreasing accuracy as the number of hops between a reference clock and its client increases. To address this problem, we might deploy many Grandmaster Clocks (GMCs). However, its financial cost is too high. To solve these problems, we propose Tiered gPTP, in which nodes synchronized by HUYGENS act as reference clocks, based on the stratum structure defined in the Network Time Protocol (NTP). We have implemented a Tiered gPTP system in OMNet++ and conducted simulation analyses to demonstrate its effectiveness. The evaluation results show that the Tiered gPTP system achieves time synchronization within 1 μs at a lower financial cost than deploying multiple GMCs.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Satellite Image Classification using Deep Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The use of satellite imagery to classify scenes is of high importance in environment monitoring, surveillance, and in analyzing the scenes with other intentions for different functions. The recent developments of Remote Sensing technologies have helped in the extraction of spatiotemporal data. Several techniques are advanced to perform automatic classification of the land scenes of remote sensing images. However, these methods are confronted with some issues when attempting to identify various scenes on the land. Heavy occlusion, complex background, objects which are too small to be recognized easily and objects of highly variable sizes are the issues which limit the models to a good degree of accuracy. In order to overcome these challenges a ResNet-50 based deep learning framework is put forward to extract global features to effectively detect the complicated land scenes. In general, this framework is divided into two limbs. There the first branch deals with preprocessed grayscale image from different scenes while the next one investigates the so-called CLAHE preprocessed features. Performance analysis of the proposed framework is carried out on two standard databases Aerial image dataset and EuroSAT. The results of empirical observations based on ResNet-50 gives the highest accuracy of the analysis for all calculated criteria, including accuracy rate, sensibility, and the specificity level compared to other similar models.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Mix-Method Approach for Efficient Waste Management using IoT-Driven Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Escalating the global waste management crisis calls for innovative technological interventions transforming the age-old practice of traditional waste handling. The present system remains mostly inefficient, labor-intensive, and environmentally unsustainable even when rising levels of urbanization and consumption of resources increase waste production. This study examines the transformative potential of IoT technologies in developing intelligent data-driven solutions for waste management to solve critical infrastructure challenges in urban centers. This study developed IoT-enabled smart waste collection systems in three metropolitan areas using a comprehensive mixed-method approach that includes quantitative sensor data analysis, geospatial mapping, and longitudinal municipal waste tracking. Advanced sensor networks and associated machine learning algorithms were used to monitor volume, composition, and efficient collections of wastes. Predictive analytics and the edge computing framework were adapted to optimize routes for better waste collection, reduce associated operational costs, and hence also minimize the environmental footprint. The key results are possible savings of 37% in waste collection costs, an increase of 42% in route optimization for collections, and a reduction of several percent in greenhouse gas emissions due to smart routing and scheduling. IoT-led strategy outperformed conventional strategies for waste management with better operational efficiency, further signifying the revolutionary changes brought by digital technologies in managing urban infrastructure.

articleTitle: Gesture Language Translation Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This study presents a revolutionary gesture language translator that can convert sign language into both text and speech output, which can aid in communication for people who are deaf or mute. This method differs from other existing alternatives in that it can convert gestures into text and voice and the other way around, from spoken words into corresponding gestures. By enabling smooth interaction between the hearing and the non-hearing, this dual-mode system improves communication. The system uses a Convolutional neural network (CNN) for gesture recognition and Flask and Python for back-end operations. Google's text-to-speech (TTS) API generates voice output, while Media-pipe is utilized to detect hand landmarks in real-time. In the opposite procedure, vocal inputs are recorded by speech recognition technology and converted into gestures using a pre-stablished sign language model. This product represents a significant achievement in the field of assistive technologies for people with speech and hearing impairments since it has a distinctive feature: two-way translation capabilities.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Learning Approaches for Workload Optimization in Cloud-Based AI Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Cloud-based AI systems operate in highly complex and dynamic environments characterized by fluctuating workloads and evolving resource demands. The scale and intricacy of these systems render traditional optimization methods—such as manual resource allocation or rule-based scheduling—inefficient and often impractical. To address these challenges, unsupervised learning techniques have emerged as powerful tools for automating workload optimization. By uncovering hidden patterns and relationships within datasets without requiring human supervision, these methods enable continuous adaptation to changing priorities and system demands. Unsupervised approaches such as clustering, anomaly detection, and dimensionality reduction have proven particularly effective in optimizing workloads. These techniques can group similar workloads, identify anomalies in resource usage, and reduce data dimensionality to improve computational efficiency. The result is a more cost-effective and performant cloud environment that supports dynamic scalability and adaptability while minimizing waste. By using unsupervised learning, organizations can enhance the operational efficiency of cloud-based AI systems, achieving superior performance and significant cost savings. Additionally, these techniques empower businesses to deliver seamless user experiences by maintaining robust and scalable infrastructures. This research underscores the pivotal role of unsupervised learning in addressing the optimization challenges modern cloud-based AI systems face. It highlights its potential to drive innovation and efficiency across various applications.

articleTitle: SkinCareNet with DermGraph: Revolutionizing Skin Cancer Detection with Adaptive Graph Intelligence Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Skin cancer detection presents significant challenges, especially in accurately distinguishing between different types of lesions. To improve detection accuracy, developed SkinCareNet with DermGraph, which addresses the limitations of traditional methods by using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to model skin lesions as graph structures. This approach captures complex spatial and relational patterns within the lesion data, going beyond the capabilities of conventional image-based techniques like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). By integrating meta-learning, the model quickly adapts to new datasets with minimal retraining, and advanced data augmentation through graph embeddings enhances its robustness. Additionally, node importance analysis improves interpretability, highlighting key areas influencing the model's decisions. Our system achieved a 98% accuracy in detecting skin cancer, offering a highly reliable and adaptable solution for clinical use.

articleTitle: Spam Classification Using Machine Learning: Performance Evaluation and Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The article discusses about using machine learning methods for determining unwanted messages. The expansion of portable phone applications has driven to an uncommon rise in SMS spam. Although considered reliable and efficient in many parts of the world, recent data clearly shows a significant increase in the volume of mobile phone spam is consistently expanding. Sorting through SMS fake is also late errand to resolve this kind of issue. The algorithms such as RandomForest,Logistic Regression and SVM are utilized to recognize spam and ham messages. The effectiveness each channel in identifying spam and legitimate messages ham is too inspected. One imperative way to reduce the issue of spam in versatile communication is to create proficient spam location algorithms.The libraries like NLTK is used for preprocessing, and distinctive calculations, , and tokenizing are all carried out.. The algorithms achieved an accuracy of 96%,97%,98% with SVM, Logistic Regression and RandomForest

articleTitle: Vigilance Alertness System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Driver fatigue and drowsiness are critical factors leading to road accidents, accounting for a significant percentage of such incidents globally. The proposed "Vigilance Alertness System" utilizes machine learning and computer vision techniques to identify driver drowsiness in instantly. By examining facial landmarks, specifically eye motions and blinks, the system assesses the driver's alertness. Machine learning enables accurate pattern recognition in facial features, while computer vision processes video frames captured via a webcam. When signs of fatigue are detected, an audio alert is triggered, prompting the driver to take timely action. This system offers a practical and efficient solution for enhancing road safety, particularly for long-distance drivers. The implemented model achieves a high detection accuracy of 95.5%, demonstrating its reliability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection using Federated Learning with Application of Federated Dropout
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The massive proliferation of IoT devices in recent years creates new challenges in securing distributed systems, especially when it comes to intrusion detection and mitigation in real-time. Most traditional cloud-based intrusion detection approaches encounter issues ranging from increased latency to bandwidths and even centralized vulnerabilities. This paper introduces an innovative IDS framework based on federated learning (FL) combined with a novel federated dropout mechanism and edge computing. Federated dropout updates model parameters selectively during communication rounds, minimizing bandwidth usage considerably without compromising model performance. This work resolves key challenges such as communication overhead and encrypted traffic processing, opening the door to strong, real-time, and decentralized security solutions.

articleTitle: Unveiling Customer Behavior: A Comprehensive Study on Predictive Models for Telcom Churn
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Predicting churn in telecoms with a range of Random Forest algorithms is a necessary and systematic way of foreseeing customers’ intention to leave the service. The research presented here focuses on telecom churn prediction by using the Random Forest algorithm, whose main objective is the early prediction of customer rejection probability. When telecom churn is indicative of how often customers abandon their relationships with companies or cut ties from service subscriptions, it has become an important subject for telecom firms to accurately predict it and best avoid it. To achieve this, a publicly available telecom customer dataset from [mention dataset source, e.g., Kaggle or UCI Machine Learning Repository] was utilized. The dataset comprises 20 independent variables and 1 target variable, with a total of 7043 rows. The data was split into a 70:30 ratio, where 70% of the data was used for training and 30% for testing. A Random Forest algorithm was applied and assessed for its capability in this predictive task. This analysis concentrates on assessing predictive accuracy, e.g., precision, recall, and F-1 scores, to determine whether the algorithm is effective in detecting potential churners early. Moreover, our study of interpretability also involves the identification of feature importance in the Random Forest framework to unveil some of the factors contributing to customer churn. The results of this paper highlight the main factors influencing churn prediction and serve as a strong foundation for telecom companies to address the problem of consumer churn. Embracing the predictive power of Random Forest could change the pace at which telecom companies lose customers, improve customer satisfaction, and ensure responsible resource utilization, ultimately fostering a sustainable business environment in a competitive market.

articleTitle: A New Maintenance Framework of WSN for Consumer and e-Commerce: A Convergence of AI, ML, and IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The aim of this study is to integrate energy-efficient wireless sensor networks (WSNs) into consumer electronics manufacturing and e-commerce systems. The study focuses on two main objectives: developing predictive maintenance machine learning (ML) models for consumer electronics production, enhancing personalization and contextualization in e-commerce platforms using energy-efficient WSN architecture. By analyzing data from sensors embedded in manufacturing processes, the predictive maintenance models predict maintenance needs, which can optimize production efficiency, reduce unscheduled downtime, and improve resource allocation. This study also investigates the financial benefits of implementing predictive maintenance strategies, showing significant cost savings and improved resource allocation. The incorporation of WSN into e-commerce systems encompasses the entire consumer electronics lifecycle. By employing an energy-efficient WSN architecture, reliable data collection for predictive maintenance is achieved while minimizing environmental impact. Within the e-commerce domain, this integration enhances customer experiences by ensuring products are delivered in optimal condition, thereby fostering customer satisfaction and loyalty. Additionally, the architecture facilitates personalization and contextualization, providing consumers with customized recommendations based on their preferences and real-time contextual information.

articleTitle: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks for AI Artwork Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The emergence of AI-made art is pioneering in the creative landscape, yet it challenges quality and authenticity across many image-generation platforms. This paper aims to develop a new AI art detector capable of checking the authenticity of artwork. The developed detector will be designed in such a way that it can evaluate essential factors regarding originality, coherence, and aesthetic appeal. This is achieved by using deep learning techniques through training over a wide variety of datasets, from those generated by AIs and humans within the context of artwork. This process will automatically identify markers that are unique to content generated by AIs. With this, the findings will provide insights into the strengths and limitations of existing AI art models, leading to improvements in the future. Commercial art production, content moderation, and intellectual property management are just some of the possible fields in which our tool can be applied by maintaining quality levels for AI-generated artworks.

articleTitle: Developing Energy-Efficient IoT Architecture with Edge and Fog Computing for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are being used in smart towns because people want more clever, efficient, and environmentally friendly systems. But the fact that these methods use a lot of energy is still a big worry. This article talks about creating an IoT design that uses less energy by using Edge and Fog Computing to make the best use of resources and boost speed in smart city apps. The suggested design uses both Edge Computing and Fog Computing. Edge devices process data locally, which means they don't need to use cloud services as much. Fog nodes bring processing even closer to the edge of the network, which ensures low delay and low energy use. The design includes energy-aware programs that make the best use of real-time energy supply and network conditions to send and process data. Our results show that smart city IoT systems actually use a lot less energy and work much more efficiently. We use a lot of models to show that moving processing from the cloud to the edge and fog layers can cut the total amount of energy needed by up to 30%. The suggested structure also guarantees very little delay in data processing, which is very important for real-time smart city applications like tracking the environment, managing traffic, and collecting trash. The results show that combining Edge and Fog Computing can make IoT systems in smart towns more energy-efficient.

articleTitle: An Efficient Hybrid Privacy Preservation Model for Big Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Personal information is an important aspect of today’s life. Big data privacy is crucial where structured and unstructured information is frequently produced, processed, and stored in large amounts. Data is increasing in various fields. As the amount of big data grows, there are multiple challenges, and preserving big data privacy is important in big data analytics. This paper summarizes various anonymization techniques for keeping big data privacy which helps to eliminate privacy risks in data preparation. Proposes a new efficient Hybrid Privacy Preservation Model (HPPM) that combines features of k-anonymity and t-closeness. The algorithm has been evaluated by applying various data privacy preservation metrics. The experimental analysis and results show that due to anonymization of data, the information loss is increased but, it preserves data privacy and accuracy of the model at a high level. The HPPM is a better anonymization technique to safeguard the quasi-identifiers and sensitive attributes that reveal user identity.

articleTitle: Development of Neural Interface-Based Brain-Controlled Robotic Prosthetics for Enhanced Mobility in Amputees
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Brain-controlled robotic devices made possible by neural interfaces are a hopeful new way to help amputees recover, as they give them more freedom and a better quality of life. Traditional prosthetics don't always offer real-time, natural control, which makes them frustrating to use and limits their abilities. This essay talks about how important it is to have prostheses that can work with the user's brain so that replacing limbs feels more normal and works better. Our goal is to create and test a neural interface technology that lets robotic replacement limbs be controlled directly from the brain. One of the ways used is creating a machine learning system to understand neural signals obtained through noninvasive electroencephalography (EEG), and these signals are then combined with a cutting-edge robotic limb. We used complex signal processing and pattern recognition techniques to figure out what the user was trying to do and make the prosthetic arm move precisely. Our system can correctly figure out different moving intents with little to no delay, according to the results. Preliminary tests with amputees showed that the new prostheses made it much easier and faster to do different jobs compared to standard ones. Participants said they were happier and more comfortable, which shows that this technology could change how prosthetics are controlled. This study lays the groundwork for future research on brain-controlled artificial systems that are scalable and easy for anyone to use. These systems could greatly assist amputees all over the world.

articleTitle: Analyzing Machine Learning Frameworks for Anomaly Detection on Web Server Log Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The field of anomaly detection has been around for decades and is still one of the most active areas of research in many fields. To build an efficient anomaly identification system, scholars and innovators must first understand the intricate configuration of data that exhibits noise, explore energetic anomaly trends, and monitor anomalies with restricted labels. Several preliminary works on anomaly detection have been developed with the advent of machine learning. This study conducts detailed explorations of deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) frameworks for anomaly sensing on web server logs. The trials comparative results will help identify suitable ML frameworks and algorithms for researchers and industrial users in anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Efficient Host Threat Detection Using The Procsage Method
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) pose a significant challenge to modern cybersecurity due to their stealth and complexity. This paper introduces a scalable host threat detection framework that utilizes provenance graphs and graph representation learning to overcome limitations of traditional defense mechanisms. By optimizing process- and thread-centric analyses within provenance graphs, the system minimizes computational overhead while maintaining robust behavioral insights. Leveraging semantic and topological feature extraction with GraphSAGE-based learning, the framework achieves precise anomaly detection via clustering techniques. Validation on benchmark datasets demonstrates substantial improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and scalability, showcasing the framework's potential for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity in Rural Areas - A Multilayered AI Approach to Combat Phishing Threats using Quantum Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Rapid advances in quantum computing have raised worries about the security of classical encryption systems, as quantum computers can break many cryptographic techniques. This research strengthens encryption algorithms against quantum-based cryptographic assaults at the convergence of cybersecurity and quantum computing. Quantum computers, using quantum parallelism and quantum algorithms like Shor's and Grover's, threaten the security of widely used cryptographic systems like RSA and ECC, which use integer factorization and discrete logarithms. Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is needed because quantum assaults can break classical encryption systems. This work emphasizes the need for quantum-resistant encryption techniques by examining the theoretical and practical effects of quantum computing on cryptography. It discusses quantum-safe algorithms like lattice-based, hash-based, and code-based cryptography that could replace or improve encryption standards. The research also examines quantum key distribution (QKD), a new secure communication method that uses quantum physics to share keys. The computational expense, implementation difficulty, and cybersecurity infrastructure integration difficulties of switching to quantum-resistant encryption methods are also examined. Quantum computing is evolving, hence safe encryption algorithms that can withstand quantum-based cryptographic assaults are needed. This paper concludes by emphasizing the need to standardize quantum-resistant algorithms, accelerate quantum cryptography research, and promote international collaboration to protect sensitive data from quantum threats. Future communication systems will depend on post-quantum cryptography to protect digital data.

articleTitle: Design and Deployment of Anti-smog Gun for clean air in Urban areas
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Around the world, travel has been challenging over the winter. The biggest issue arises, though, when fog and air particles mix to create smog, which is denser than fog and reduces visibility. The goal of this project is to enhance urban air quality by creating and utilizing a revolutionary anti-smog cannon. The cannon disperses water or anti-smog chemicals in a targeted way using special equipment such as mist-generating devices, precise nozzle designs, pump mechanisms, and advanced control systems. The study examines the ideation, prototyping, testing, and optimization phases of the development of the gun and emphasizes the necessity for such strategy for urban environments. The evaluation focuses on performance indicators such as environmental impact, pressure regulation, droplet size distribution, and dispersion coverage. Conducted field experiments and real-world deployments offer important insights into the gun's effectiveness in reducing pollutants and improving air quality. The creation and use of the anti-smog gun marks a major breakthrough in the campaigns for clean air and the battle against urban air pollution.

articleTitle: Building AI-Driven Frameworks for Real-Time Threat Detection and Mitigation in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The fast growth of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has made security risks more complicated and numerous. To find and stop these threats in real time, we need new and creative solutions. This article talks about an AI-powered system that can make IoT networks safer by finding and stopping threats as they happen. The system uses both machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) to look at real-time data from IoT devices and find strange patterns that could be signs of an attack. This is done by using advanced algorithms, like decision trees, neural networks, and reinforcement learning, to learn new things all the time and adjust to new dangers. To improve the efficiency of identification and cut down on false positives, a mixed method is used that combines controlled and unstructured learning. The system also has an automatic mitigating procedure that separates infected devices and stops them from doing more damage when risks are found. Compared to standard security methods, our results show that the proposed structure makes danger identification and prevention much more effective in IoT networks. The system is very good at finding different kinds of threats, like DDoS, malware, and illegal access, and it does this while using very little computing power. This means it can be used in IoT settings with limited resources. This study provides a flexible and scalable way to protect the IoT environment, which is becoming more and more linked.

articleTitle: EfficientHACoTNet: A New Framework for Detecting Grape Leaf Diseases with Depthwise Separable Convolutions and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Grapevine diseases are one of the major challenges in the viticulture industry, affecting not only the yield but also the quality of grapes. Timely and precise identification is essential for managing diseases and maintaining optimal crop health. This study presents EfficientHACoTNET, an innovative deep learning framework specifically developed for the efficient detection of diseases in grape leaves. The model utilizes depth-wise separable convolutions (DSC) to reduce computational complexity and attention mechanisms to enhance feature extraction from leaf images by striking a balance between high accuracy and computational efficiency. EfficientHACoTNET is built to work seamlessly on edge devices, making it a practical choice for real-time monitoring in precision agriculture. Extensive experiments conducted on specialized grape leaf disease datasets reveal that the proposed model outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in terms of both detection accuracy and inference speed. These findings underscore the potential of EfficientHACoTNET as a powerful tool for detecting major grapevine diseases, providing practical solutions for precision viticulture.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning for PCOS Detection and femBot: A Novel NLP-Based Menstrual Health Chatbot for Women’s Health Support
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: An increase in the incidence of reproductive health disorders has made the need for innovative approaches in the area of timely diagnosis as well as health education imperative. One of the most prevalent forms of reproductive health disorder is Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS). PCOS often goes undiagnosed and has vague symptoms, making it a potential risk for the long-term adverse effects of infertility and metabolic disorders. It is unlikely that traditional methods of diagnosis will be accessible in underserved places. This paper discusses an integrated approach combining machine learning (ML) for PCOS detection and a natural language processing (NLP)-powered chatbot, femBot, for the awareness of menstrual health. Nine ML models were utilized, including random forest, support vector machines, and others, out of which XGBoost scored the highest accuracy of 96.33%. The femBot chatbot was developed using a sequential model that effectively responds to user queries in a test with an accuracy of 83.08%. These two technologies are accessible and provide accurate personalized health support so that healthcare outcomes can be extended to populations that have poor infrastructure. The proposed models show the power of ML and NLP combined to improve women's health care by facilitating early diagnosis and health education. The future directions will be the realization and implementation of both systems into a coherent health platform named FemWell for women's health support and education.

articleTitle: Identification of Hub Genes and Enriched Pathways in Lung Cancer using Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This research analyzes RNA sequencing data collected from individual cell data from the GSE127471 and GSE245170 datasets to identify potential biomarkers and treatment targets in non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC). The analysis pipeline, implemented in Google Colab using Python libraries like Scanpy and Scvelo, involves data preprocessing, reducing dimensionality, grouping of cells, and examining differential gene expression. We identified key genes utilizing the study of networks that involve interactions among proteins and executed pathway enrichment analysis using gseapy. Key hub genes, such as RPS27A, RPL13, and EEF1A1, and enriched pathways, including ribosome biogenesis and translation, were identified. These findings highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for NSCLC. Further validation through literature search using pymed revealed existing evidence supporting the role of these genes and pathways in lung cancer. Our study demonstrates the utility of bioinformatics tools for the recognition of possible treatment targets and biomarkers for complex diseases like NSCLC.

articleTitle: Shielding Software: The Vital Role of Headers in Ensuring Application Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: In an era where cyber threats loom large, the safeguarding of software applications is paramount. This paper delves into the indispensable role played by headers in fortifying application security. Headers, integral components of HTTP requests and responses, serve as gatekeepers regulating communication between clients and servers. Through meticulous analysis and case studies, this research elucidates how headers serve as a frontline defense mechanism, thwarting various cyber-attacks such as XSS, CSRF and command injection attacks. Furthermore, this paper explores the multifaceted aspects of headers, encompassing CSP Header, HSTS Header, and other security directives. By implementing robust header configurations, organizations can erect formidable barriers against unauthorized access, data breaches, and other security breaches. Additionally, the paper discusses emerging trends and best practices in header management, highlighting the significance of continuous monitoring and updates to adapt to evolving threats.

articleTitle: Dynamic StarCraft: Multi-Agent Generative AI for Immersive Experiences
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The present research reveals a unique educational approach through the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) with the focus on storytelling with children. It is shown that by adding GenAI narrative co-creation, voice-over synthesis, and video audition to the system, the learning process becomes interesting. We understand how the audience creates the stories with which they will perform, how the stories are narrated in audio created with advanced text-to-speech systems, and how images for the narratives are generated with text-to-video. Our assessment is however concerned with the level of the languages used in writing the stories, how the stories written were pronounced and the images that were produced, as we point out the ability of the tool to entertain young learners.

articleTitle: Bluetooth Vulnerabilities and Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Bluetooth technology, which facilitates wireless communication between Billions of devices including smartphones, tablets, laptops, and Internet of Thing (IoT) devices, is a cornerstone of modern connectivity. Its importance lies in its ability to enable seamless data exchange and interaction across a wide range of applications, from personal gadgets to complex industrial systems. Despite its widespread adoption, Bluetooth is not immune to critical security vulnerabilities. Issues like Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) vulnerabilities and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks can overwhelm devices with excessive traffic, while BLE Forced Connection can lead to unauthorized access, and eavesdropping exposes sensitive data being exchanged. We have discussed these vulnerabilities in detail, examining their mechanisms, potential impacts, and various implementation aspects. Additionally, we have added demonstrations to illustrate how these attacks can be executed and the potential consequences. To prevent these threats, we explored essential measures, including regular firmware updates, secure pairing protocols, and careful management of Bluetooth settings. Adopting best practices like disabling Bluetooth when not in use and monitoring connected devices can further enhance security, ensuring the reliable and safe operation of the vast and growing ecosystem of Bluetooth-enabled devices.

articleTitle: Optimizing construction and demolition waste Segmentation using Advanced Deep Learning Techniques (Semantic vs Instance segmentation)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Rapid urbanization has accelerated the generation of C&D wastes in large quantities, therefore, leading to environmental as well as economic issues. The conventional methods of segregating wastes by hand and evaluating volumes are inefficient and susceptible to errors; therefore, an automated method is desired. This paper evaluates whether deep learning-based segmentation models can be used to study C&D waste, primarily focusing on concrete, tiles, and bricks. The two models that are used are a U-Net-based model for semantic segmentation and Mask R-CNN for instance segmentation. Mask R-CNN gave better performance with better accuracy in segmentation and was also consistent up to 5500 annotated images and provided better results in detailed irregular shapes. The U-Net-based model performed relatively well in semantic segmentation but failed in the case of complex structures where instance-level differentiation is required. Both models were further optimized with Optuna in hyper parameters, which allowed increasing their accuracy. In summary, these results show Mask R-CNN to be a more effective tool for detailed waste segmentation, leading to significant implications for improvement of recycling processes and reductions of environmental impacts.

articleTitle: Defense Mechanism to Thwart Model Poisoning on Non-IID Data based Federated Learning for Credit Fraud Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The ever-growing sophistication of credit fraud, encompassing methods like identity theft, necessitates robust detection mechanisms. While machine learning algorithms analyze transaction data for fraud patterns, they struggle with complex schemes, fairness, and privacy concerns. This paper proposes a federated learning approach to address these challenges, leveraging the inherent heterogeneity of transaction data. By partitioning data based on merchant categories and geographical regions, this approach enables collaborative model training tailored to each category’s unique characteristics without compromising data privacy. Moreover, federated learning adapts models to diverse transaction contexts, effectively addressing the non-IID nature of the data and enhancing fraud detection across different segments. Furthermore, countermeasures against model poisoning attacks are incorporated to ensure the integrity and efficacy of the overall system.

articleTitle: Innovations in Robotics and Automation to Improve Efficiency and Precision in Healthcare Delivery and Rehabilitation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Adding robots and automation to healthcare delivery and therapy systems is changing the medical field by making care for patients faster and more accurate. This essay looks at some new developments in robots that are changing the way healthcare is provided, especially in recovery settings. Robotics-based systems make it possible for very accurate diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation techniques, which help patients do better and heal faster. For example, robotic surgery makes it possible to do minimally invasive treatments more precisely, which lowers the risk of problems and speeds up the healing process. Robotic exoskeletons and other assistance devices are used in rehabilitation to provide personalized, adaptable treatments that help people regain their movement faster and with less need for heavy physical involvement. Automation in healthcare also includes monitoring systems, where AI-powered robots can look at huge amounts of medical data and make accurate diagnoses quickly to help doctors make decisions. Automated systems for tracking patients and managing medications also make sure that care is given on time, which lowers the risk of mistakes and increases patient safety. The study also talks about how machine learning and AI can be used to create self-learning robots that can change their behavior based on the needs of each patient. By looking at the newest developments in robotics and automation, this study shows how healthcare costs could be cut by a lot, care could be made easier to get, and quality of care could be raised. When robots, the Internet of Things (IoT), and AI come together, they could open up new ways to keep an eye on people's health, do treatments from afar, and make medicine more personalized.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Brain-Computer Interface for Robotic System Control Using Right-Left Hand Movements with Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: In this work, machine learning models are utilized to interpret EEG data for the development of a brain-computer interface (BCI) system that controls a robotic car. Voluntary hand motor actions are employed for interface controls, with each hand corresponding to a different direction. EEG data is recorded using a 14-channel EMOTIV EPOC+ device during motor activities such as moving the car left, right, or stopping. The raw EEG signals are preprocessed using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) before training a range of models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, Bi-Directional GRU, Transformer-based, and a Stacking Ensemble Technique (SET). The highest accuracy is achieved by SET (87%), followed by XGBoost (82%). These results demonstrate the robustness of ensemble approach SET for EEG-based tasks. Although further advancements in real-time processing are necessary, the system's ability to successfully control the robotic car underscores the potential of BCIs in robotic control and assistive systems development.

articleTitle: Meta Emotional Intelligence for Early Bone Abnormality Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This research addresses the imperative for early detection of bone abnormalities through the innovative integration of meta-emotional intelligence. Meta-emotional intelligence, a high level of emotional understanding encompassing both personal and others' emotions, is explored for its potential link to bone health. Current evidence suggests a correlation between meta-emotional intelligence and bone diseases, emphasizing the need for advanced technologies in early detection. Approximately 1.5 million individuals suffer from bone diseases, making early detection crucial. Existing methods for bone abnormality detection include neuro-cognitive models, deep learning frameworks, and sentiment analysis, each with limitations. To overcome these, a novel approach is proposed, combining image and text classification models. The image classification model employs a Convolutional Neural Network on X-ray images, achieving an 86% accuracy rate. Simultaneously, a text classification model analyzes emotional content to predict bone abnormalities with promising results. The fusion of both models presents a holistic approach, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and contributing to proactive healthcare interventions. The integration of meta-emotional intelligence provides a unique perspective, bridging emotional expressions and physiological conditions for early intervention, personalized healthcare, and improved patient outcomes

articleTitle: AI Powered Plant Disease Detection and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Certain plant diseases cause extensive damage in agriculture; this leads results in a huge loss, and poses a major risk to food security. In general, conventional techniques of diagnosing these diseases are time- consuming, expensive and depend solely on human operator’s experience. As part of this study, we suggest an entirely new architecture for disease detection, diagnostics, and remedies using Ensemble Learning, Generative AI, and, Explainable AI (XAI). It combines deep learning method Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Random Forest classifiers and transformer-based generative models to give diagnosis and suggest treatment processes. LIME and heat plots of attention make the behavior of the system clear to users and contribute to the perfect implementation of artificial intelligence technology in agriculture. This framework is also both timely and suitable for the development and practice of sustainable agriculture especially in the developing world where professional input on agriculture is hard to come by.

articleTitle: Computer Vision-Based Hand Recognition and Gesture Control for Dino Games
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Hand Recognition and Gesture Control For Dino Game Using Computer Vision to control the popular Chrome Dino game using hand recognition and gesture control through computer vision techniques. The system leverages real-time image processing and machine learning algorithms to detect and interpret hand gestures, allowing for an intuitive and interactive gaming experience. The proposed method utilizes a webcam to capture live video feed, from which hand landmarks are extracted using a pre-trained neural network model. Various hand gestures, such as swipe and hold, are then mapped to corresponding in-game actions such as jumping and ducking. This gesture-based control mechanism not only enhances user engagement but also demonstrates the potential of computer vision in creating touchless interfaces for gaming applications.

articleTitle: GenAI based Data Extraction with Query-Based Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: An innovative method has been proposed to enhance data extraction and analysis from PDF files by combining OCR technology with advanced AI models. The process begins with a PDF Reader module that employs OCR to extract text from PDFs, addressing challenges posed by the unstructured nature of document content. To tackle these difficulties, the Gemini LLM model transforms semi-structured or unstructured text into structured JSON formats. Once the data is structured, the Pandas AI component leverages the GROQ and Mistral LLM models to generate visualizations such as charts, graphs, and tables. These visual representations provide a more intuitive and insightful way to interpret the extracted data. This approach not only ensures more accurate data extraction but also significantly enhances the analysis and comprehension of complex documents.

articleTitle: EXAMSENTRY: Secure, Verify, Excel
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: In today’s digital world, online assessments are essential for companies to evaluate candidates effectively. However, they face challenges like malpractice and test integrity. We aim to create a scalable, secure platform that ensures fairness and reliability in online evaluations. The platform monitors the test environment by blocking browser extensions and media interference while verifying participants’ identities using advanced methods. Eye tracking will ensure that candidates stay focused on the screen, while the system checks the stability of their internet connection and browser settings. Artificial intelligence will detect suspicious behavior during the exam, and cloud infrastructure will manage high user traffic for smooth performance under heavy loads. Results will be automatically generated and securely delivered to companies, providing a comprehensive solution for large-scale assessments.

Author Keywords: application development in the education domain

articleTitle: Using Quantum Annealing to Solve Large-Scale Optimization Problems in Logistics and Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: In planning and scheduling, large-scale optimization problems often have complex limits and a lot of factors, which makes them hard to answer with standard methods. Quantum annealing has become a hopeful way to deal with these problems because it can quickly look into a lot of possible solutions. This essay looks into how quantum annealing might be used to solve optimization problems in transportation and scheduling, with a focus on how it could be used for route planning, inventory management, and arranging workers. To do these optimization jobs, quantum annealing is used. This is a quantum computing method that gets the global minimum of a cost function. We use the D-Wave quantum annealer in this method. It turns the problem's limits and objective function into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. The quantum annealer then works on this model to find the best answers. The suggested method combines traditional preparation methods with quantum annealing to get the best results for big schedule and transportation issues. We use quantum annealing to solve difficult multi-objective optimization problems, like reducing shipping time, cost, and resource use all at the same time. Preliminary results show that quantum annealing can make solutions much better and use computers much more efficiently than traditional methods for optimizing supplies and schedules. Quantum annealing works especially well with problems that have a lot of dimensions. It can provide scalable answers that sometimes work better than standard methods.

articleTitle: An Associative Memory Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder is one of the greatest challenges in diagnosis because it manifests in different forms and does not have a specific medical diagnostic test. With the rapid increase in ASD cases worldwide, the need for accurate and accessible diagnostic tools has increased the manifold. This paper discusses how Bidirectional Associative Memory can be used in the diagnosis of ASD, focusing on its ability to map relationships between input characteristics and diagnostic outcomes. Robustness against noisy and incomplete data creates a unique advantage for BAM in using real-world medical applications. The methodology includes rigorous data preprocessing, feature selection, and bidirectional mapping to help improve the diagnostic accuracy in a way that is interpretable. The model’s applicability and reliability are confirmed using comprehensive evaluation with performance metrics such as accuracy, AUC-ROC, and classification reports. The results thus emphasize that only through integrating innovative models of machine learning with clinical workflows could one possibly facilitate timely intervention and improved patient care for ASD.

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical IOT data using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The potential of blockchain technology is very high in terms of transforming healthcare management systems, especially in safety, interoperability, and the integrity of health data. This revolutionary ability comes from the decentralized and immutable nature of blockchain architecture that enhances secure transactions. The implementation of SHA-256 algorithm greatly strengthens data against malicious attacks. This ensures that it cannot be hacked into unauthorized hands for sensitive information of patients. The use of smart contracts along with existing health data formats improves interoperability among various healthcare systems. Such level of interoperability increases both the communication and the swapping of health information across different platforms. However, the introduction of blockchain in healthcare faces several challenges about acceptance by users, scalability to ensure workability, and compliance with regulatory standards. A good insight related to the emerging landscape in which healthcare data management takes place can be derived from the present study. This can be achieved by studying the potential benefits blockchain technology would bring along with its integration into health management systems and the challenges that may come up in the process.

articleTitle: Human Perceptual Biases and their Analogous Prevalence in Artificial Intelligence Systems: Bias Mitigation for Dependable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is entering and influencing all facets of our life. Unintended bias in these AI systems can have serious consequences and are of great concern. We have made tremendous progress in the field of AI by studying the various nuances of human intelligence spanning the metaphysical to the physiological perspectives. Deep Learning was inspired by the structure of neurons in the human brain. Similarly, a study of the shortcomings and fallibility of human intelligence will help us design dependable AI systems that are robust, reliable, and safe. With this in mind, this study uses findings from Psychophysics for some of the most common human perceptual biases in magnitude estimation (viz. Regression effect, Range effect, Scalar Variability, and Sequential effect) to check for their analogous prevalence in four Machine Learning (ML) models based on Support Vector Machines, LSTM, CNN-GRU, and Transformers, for stock market price prediction task. We found that the ML models, which are assumed to be objective and immune to emotions, can be as biased as humans. The paper discusses the implications of these biases in general and shows methods for their mitigation using data augmentation and synthetic data generated using Wasserstein GAN, which also suggests that a Bayesian framework may explain the presence of these biases.

articleTitle: LSTM Networks for Improved Environmental Monitoring and Biodiversity Conservation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Understanding and managing the effects of climate change and loss of biodiversity are crucial. However, traditional approaches are largely ineffective in dealing with these challenges because environmental data is complex and uncertain. Environmental monitoring thus comes into play. To this end, this paper presents an investigation into the LSTM network, a type of recurrent neural network that was developed to capture long-range patterns in sequential data. With the ability of LSTM networks to process historical data and understand temporal relationships, the prediction of climate variables like temperature, precipitation, and extreme weather occurrences is now much more advanced. As a result, this has led to the development of more accurate climate models, which are essential for creating mitigation and adaptation plans for climate change. Analyzing time-series data, LSTM networks can mimic species population dynamics and habitat changes in biodiversity conservation. This is helpful in predicting future population trends and identifying critical times of vulnerability. This ability allows for timely and effective conservation. Huge environmental datasets are collected and preprocessed, the models' excellent performance in environmental monitoring tasks is further proved by their 97.6% accuracy. A network of LSTM is established with the aim of improving the accuracy of environment-science forecasting and enhancing associated decision-making processes, which eventually lead to more resilient and sustainable resources management.

articleTitle: Algorithmic Optimization of Coupon Pooling Application: A Machine Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The accumulation of unused coupons poses a significant challenge in the modern era, driven by technological advancements and growing environmental consciousness. This paper presents the Coupon Pooling App, a platform enabling users to buy and sell coupons. The app leverages Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology to extract essential details such as coupon codes, expiry dates, and categories, and employs machine learning algorithms to power its recommendation system—a central focus of this study. By utilizing OCR-extracted data, the app generates personalized coupon suggestions, addressing the issue of wasted coupons while unlocking their latent value. This innovation promotes resource efficiency, supports sustainability, and enhances practical savings.

articleTitle: Improving Artificial English Academic Paper Summarization employing Cutting-Edge Transformer Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: English Academic Paper Summarization entails the process of converting certain scholarly document into summarized but coherent overviews where/profiles of data and/or relationships in the original texts are conserved. Given the constant increase in scholarly work, literature summarization remains vital for researchers to become aware of new discoveries. Previous studies have mapped summary production with the practical difficulties involved in parsing academic language and document structures, resulting in basic or contextually irrelevant summaries. To address these challenges, we propose to adopt and further optimize the roBERTa transformer model for academic summarization in this study. The approach, which optimizes roBERTa, delivers an amazing level of accuracy of 99.5% coupled with high accuracy and recall metrics suggesting the methods applicability to generate contextually accurate summaries. The model is implemented in Python programming language. With the comprehensive assessment on real-world academic dataset, our study expounds that roBERTa is capable of generating accurate, domain-specific and comprehensive summaries while maintaining such important details and terms. The outcomes help to progress the development of natural language processing in the academic environment and increase the efficiency of knowledge transfer to scholars and industry specialists due to the enhancement of the availability and application of academic research.

articleTitle: Algorithm For Preprocessing Satellite Imagery That Uses Geometric, Atmospheric, And Radiometric Correction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: In the last few years, the topic of remote sensing image processing has gained a lot of interest. Object identification, picture categorization, and image retrieval are all included in satellite image processing. Because satellite data can take detailed, large-scale images of the Earth's surface over time, it can be a valuable tool for understanding and managing both natural and artificial ecosystems.
