Due to a variety of circumstances, such as atmospheric disruption, absorption, scene illumination, satellite orbit motion, and geometrical distribution, raw images obtained from various satellite sensors frequently exhibit distortion and inconsistency. To ensure proper analysis, satellite images must be preprocessed effectively to remove distortions and improve image quality. In order to preprocess raw landslide satellite photos, this study presents a deep learning framework that combines advanced deep learning techniques with more traditional methods including noise reduction, geometry correction, atmospheric correction, radiometric correction, and image enhancement. Preprocessing improves image clarity and inconsistency, which increases dataset accuracy. This work also provides a quick overview of several satellite picture defects and demonstrates how preprocessing greatly enhances landslide detection analysis. This method provides a significant advancement in the preprocessing of satellite data, enabling more intelligent geographic decision-making.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of 2D Images into 3D Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Due to the fast pace of evolution and development, there has been enormous advancement in almost every sector. Every advancement is meant to reduce human efforts, costs, and time. The transformation of 2D images into 3D is central to achieving this goal. Generating a 3D representation from 2D images with utmost realism poses a fundamental challenge in the realms of image-based modeling and computer vision. Current studies frequently emphasize the design of the point cloud generation network, neglecting the extraction of features from 2D images and minimizing loss during feature propagation in the network. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel framework for high-fidelity recovery of object shapes from 2D images. The proposed approach utilizes the single-view neural implicit shape representations to leverage explicit 3D shape supervision. The single-stage network structure can reduce the loss of the extracted 2D image features. The paper examines classical computer vision techniques and others, stating their advantages and limitations while providing in-depth descriptions of the methodologies being used. By illuminating different approaches, this article serves as an insightful guide to the various strategies and models shaping the conversion of 2D photos into their respective 3D representations, contributing to the ongoing debate on technological advancements.

articleTitle: Dynamic Vehicle Stability Analysis Using IoT Sensors and Bayesian Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: A new way to improve vehicle stability analysis is to combine IoT sensors with sophisticated analytical methods like Bayesian networks. It investigates how to use Bayesian networks to handle data collected in real-time by Internet of Things (IoT) sensors mounted on vehicles. A Bayesian network model is built using data from sensors that measure things like acceleration, yaw rate, wheel speed, and road conditions to calculate the probability of a vehicle's stability during dynamic maneuvers. One important part of this project is building a framework for Bayesian networks that can make decisions and infer things in real time using sensor data. Evaluate the model's capacity to forecast possible stability problems through simulation and practical testing, including understeer or oversteer. It tests the IoT sensor network in various settings to see how well it scales and adapts. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method is practical and effective in enhancing vehicle performance and safety via proactive stability control. IoT sensor integration with Bayesian networks provides a powerful approach to real-time data analysis and monitoring, which helps develop smart transport systems and vehicle safety technology.

articleTitle: Integrating Imaging and Clinical Data for Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: That disorder affecting the nervous system, Parkinson's disorder can worsen with time and cause a host of health problems. Parkinson's disease diminishes cerebral function and may induce physical complications in senior individuals. Parkinson's disease can induce a range of disorders by impairing neurological in nature, behavioral, and physiological systems. Physical structures exhibit minimal damage at early diagnosis, complicating the prediction of Parkinson's illness in its initial stages based solely on physical observation. Recent studies on electroencephalogram (EEG) signs in the identification of Parkinson's illness have revealed significant aspects pertinent to early detection. Electroencephalography (EEG) is a multifaceted signal comprising several non-linear and non-stationary elements. Subsequently, an auto-encoder-based deep extraction of features method is employed to derive the spatial and temporal attributes from the four frequency partitions. Additionally, statistical and spectral attributes are obtained. The gathered attributes are utilized to analyze notable patterns associated with Parkinson's disease. Optimal weighted feature fusion is achieved through the precise adjustment of weights. The proposed DLB-LSTM (Densely Located Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory) employs weighted features so that we can identify PD. To impede the progression of Parkinson's disease, the algorithm autonomously learns from the signals and delivers targeted outcomes.

articleTitle: Autoencoder-LSTM Ensembles for Predictive Analysis of Financial Churn Patterns
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: In the financial sector, customer churn is a significant problem that influences the organization’s revenue growth. Churn means that customers have left their current providers which is a negative factor for the providers or financial institutions; therefore, accurate churn prediction helps institutions to increase customer loyalty and satisfaction by improving the quality of service. In this paper, a new method of using Autoencoder and LSTM network for predicting financial churn patterns is introduced. The Autoencoder is used to reduce dimensions and for unsupervised learning acts as a pass through that allows the model to learn the latent patterns in customer behaviour and transactions. Since the LSTM has demonstrated its efficacy in analyzing temporal dependencies of a sequence in time series, it is used to predict churn by analyzing sequential customer activity. The ensemble approach combines the merits of the two models improving the predictive power and especially the stability in a situation of data scarcity and high noise levels. Experimental comparison with conventional predictive models such as decision trees and logistic regression reveal that the Autoencoder-LSTM is more accurate and sensitive than traditional models by comparison. In other words, the proposed model enhances the early identification of potential churners and such institutions can then take appropriate measures of containing it, and in the process, offer relevant retention solutions. The paper describes the benefits of utilizing deep learning models for churn prediction for the financial industry and provides information on how such methods might be used to improve customer retention. Possible future research avenues consist of improving the model interpretability and generalizing the approach to other industries with comparable churn prediction requirements. The accuracy obtained from the proposed method is higher at 99.7% compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Classification and Labeling Techniques of Educational Resources Based on BERT-CNN model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The key factor in promoting accessibility and improving the educational experience is accurate classification and labelling of educational materials. Research paper presents a novel approach to educational material classification that makes use of BERT-CNN, a hybrid model that combines and CNNs. The limitations of conventional approaches are addressed by research methodology, which seamlessly integrates a contextual understanding of BERT with CNN's extraction capabilities to address the prior difficulty. It has frequently been difficult for prior techniques to properly capture category elements and comprehend contextual complexities in educational text classification. Here, research leverage the pre-trained contextual embeddings of BERT to enable research model to capture complicated semantics in educational texts, and the CNN architecture successfully extracts categorical features from these embeddings. By combining these two potent models, research is able to capture the logical and structural characteristics of educational resources and create a thorough knowledge of them. Furthermore, research implementation in Python makes use of well-known deep learning packages like TensorFlow and PyTorch, guaranteeing repeatability and accessibility for practitioners and researchers. Research suggested model performs very well, achieving 99% classification accuracy through extensive manipulation and analysis of datasets on various educational resources. The findings demonstrate the efficiency and resilience of research approach in correctly categorizing and labelling instructional materials, underscoring its significance in the management of educational content and strategic enhancement.

articleTitle: Binary Learning Cooking Algorithm with Relief for Feature Selection of High-dimensional Gene Expression Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Feature selection (FS) has a significant impact on machine learning. The objective is to find the most important features while maintaining high classification accuracy by identifying the possible fewest features from the high-dimensional dataset. Researchers prefer to use the filter-wrapper model by considering different metaheuristic methods for accurate feature selection. But in some cases, the proposed algorithms become less productive and achieve high time complexity. This paper presents a hybrid model of Relief with Binary Learning Cooking Algorithm (BLCA) to select optimal features. The algorithm builds on the Learning cooking algorithm (BLCA), a new optimization method inspired by the learning process "How to learn cooking". We tested how well this method responds to FS challenges in high-dimensional datasets using six cancer datasets, many with different ranges of features. We compared different existing FS algorithms with R-BLCA using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F-Score. The results show that the proposed algorithm performs better than other FS methods with an accuracy of 99. 91% for the SRBCT dataset.

articleTitle: Automated Fire Suppression System for Electrical Panel Enclosures Using Iot and Embedded System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The Automated Fire Suppression System for Electrical Panel Enclosures presents an advanced IoT-driven solution for industrial fire safety, focusing on real-time hazard detection and automated suppression. By integrating high-precision temperature and gas sensors with an STM32 microcontroller for data processing and a NodeMCU module for Wi-Fi communication, the system ensures immediate detection and response to fire risks. Upon hazard identification, the system autonomously activates a relay-controlled fire extinguisher, significantly reducing response time and minimizing damage to critical assets. Real-time alerts are sent to personnel via email, while detailed incident data is logged in Google Sheets for traceability and compliance. Designed with cost-effective, scalable components, the system integrates seamlessly into existing infrastructures, enhancing operational efficiency, supporting continuous safety monitoring, and reducing human intervention. This paper explores the system's architecture, implementation, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its potential to transform fire safety practices in high-risk industrial environments. This research also highlights the system's adaptability to various industrial applications, showcasing its potential for widespread deployment in diverse environments requiring robust fire safety measures.

articleTitle: Simulation and Evaluation of a DWDM System Utilizing OptiSystem
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: A framework for optical fiber transmission called Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) uses evenly distributed light frequencies to send multiple data at once. This provides a workable method for growing the current system's capacity. The multi-channel fiber communication technology in existence today aims to illustrate the paradigm of communication via DWDM by covering up an increasing amount of data in order to send and receive an extended length of communication frame- work. Utilizing Opti System simulation software, we conducted an examination of a 32 x 40 GB/s the entirety of a DWDM communication fiber of 50 km utilizing Bit rate for Various Channel Single-Mode Fiber (SMF) Positioning by employing dispersion compensating fiber as a compensator, dispersion can be fully compensated for. This investigation investigates the general implementation of 40 Gbps bit-rate 32 channel DWDM communication.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Security in Transmission Through Quantum Key Distribution in Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: As the world becomes more computerized, keeping data transfer safe has become very important. Quantum computers and other strong computers have the ability to break classical encryption methods, even though they are widely used. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a new way to protect data. It uses quantum physics to make sure that the sharing of cryptographic keys is safe. The aim of this study is to look into how QKD can be used to improve the security of data transfer. The suggested method combines QKD with current encryption standards to create a safe and effective way to send data. The method includes setting up a key sharing system based on QKD and then using symmetric encryption algorithms to keep the data being sent safe. The system is tried in different communication settings to see how well it protects against spying and "man-in-the-middle" attacks. The study's results show that QKD greatly improves the safety of sending data by keeping the cryptography keys secret. The results show that QKD has the potential to stop people from getting in without permission and find any attempts to change the keys while they are being sent out. The table below shows performance numbers that show how well QKD works in real-world situations. It shows how well communication speeds and security measures compare.

articleTitle: Integrating Reinforcement Learning with Explainable AI for Real-Time Decision Making in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Combining Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Explainable AI (XAI) is becoming more popular as a way to improve making decisions in real time in settings that are always changing. RL lets systems learn the best policies on their own because it can adapt to changes that are hard to predict. However, the fact that RL models aren't completely clear makes them hard to use in important situations where decision clarity is very important. This problem can be fixed with XAI methods that give us readable information about how decisions are made. This builds trust and responsibility. This paper looks at a system that combines RL and XAI to help people make better decisions in places where things change quickly and there is a lot of doubt. We use a deep Q-learning method to teach agents how to behave in changing situations like self-navigation and allocating resources. For later understanding, we use SHAP (SHapley Additive Explanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations). Benchmark dynamic datasets and real-world case studies are used to test the system. The results show that adding XAI makes RL rules easier to understand without hurting performance. People who have a stake in the system can better understand and change how it works with the help of decision explanations. When compared to standard RL models, the results show that decisions are 15% more likely to be right and mistake rates are 20% lower. Combining RL and XAI has the ability to make strong, understandable systems that can make flexible decisions in real time in complex settings.

articleTitle: Milk Adulteration Detection Through Statistical Analysis, Spectroscopy, & AI Integration Footsteps
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Milk adulteration, particularly by adding water, is a common problem that impacts both the quality and safety of milk. This study focuses on detecting water adulteration in milk using Mid-Infrared (MIR) spectroscopy and AI-based analysis. A total of 100 milk samples were prepared, with 1 mL of water added to each sample. The MIR sensor was used to collect data by measuring how the milk absorbed light at various wavelengths. To ensure accuracy, all tests were conducted in a controlled environment. The collected data showed distinct patterns for each milk sample, which were then analyzed using statistical methods to detect water adulteration levels. The method was tested for accuracy, with promising results showing that it can reliably identify adulteration. This approach provides a quick and efficient way to detect milk adulteration, which could enhance quality control in the dairy industry. Additionally, the success rate of this technique was evaluated, proving the method's accuracy and effectiveness in identifying even small amounts of added water. The method is straightforward and easy to implement for practical use. Some Artificial Intelligence (AI) based methods are discussed which the next extension for the adulteration detection.

Author Keywords: AI for Milk Adulterant detection footsteps

articleTitle: Text2Image: Generating Visuals from Words using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Transforming text into images represents a major leap in technology, unlocking new possibilities in sectors like design, marketing, and education. While models such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Diffusion Models have shown progress, they still face difficulties in generating diverse and accurate visual content.This project explores the use of deep learning to develop a system that converts textual descriptions into visuals, focusing on GANs and Diffusion Models. By training the models on large datasets containing paired text and images, we aim to enhance their ability to interpret text and generate high-quality visuals. Preliminary results suggest that the models produce visually appealing images that generally match the input text, though precision in fine details remains a challenge. This project demonstrates the potential of deep learning to bridge the gap between text and image generation, offering valuable applications in various industries.

articleTitle: Dynamic Load Balancing in Cloud Computing Using a Hybrid Bidirectional LSTM-RNN with Deep Learning VM Snapshot Protocols
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Dynamic load balancing is the ability in cloud computing to distribute workload across multiple virtual machine (VM), such that the performance of overall performance and resource utilization can be optimized. The proposed system introduces a new hybrid approach of using a Hybrid Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory RNN (BILSTM-RNN) and a Deep Learning-based VM snapshot Protocol. This approach dynamically schedules tasks in real time based on the prediction of task execution time, task resource requirement and task-VM allocation. This model, therefore, allows the Hybrid Bidirectional LSTM RNN to identify temporal trends in the workload allocation and accurately assign tasks the VM Snapshot Protocol to compensate for system restoration and VM state transfer, increasing the systems transferability of lift-ups and downwards-levelling. The system also leverages these deep learning techniques for better load balancing, quicker processing lags, and throughput. Extensive simulations in a cloud environment show that this model surpasses traditional load balancing algorithms in task scheduling efficiency, scalability, and response time reduction, making it well-suited for large-scale, diverse cloud infrastructures.

Author Keywords: Deep Learning Hybrid Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network (BiLSTM RNN)

articleTitle: Multi-Model Deep Learning Framework for Autonomous Perception and Scene Understanding
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Autonomous perception and scene understanding is a crucial task when it comes to groundbreaking inventions such as autonomous vehicles (AVs). AVs are capable of understanding their surroundings and determining what to do on their own. However, an essential aspect of ensuring their reliability is understanding the certainty of their predictions. This paper addresses the above by introducing a probabilistic approach that can estimate the model’s certainty in its predictions. Additionally, it proposes a new model specifically designed to evaluate prediction certainty. It also presents a comparative study of many state-of-the-art approaches aimed at improving autonomous perception technologies.

articleTitle: DST-M2D: A Dualistic-Series Transformer Framework for Major Depressive Disorder Analysis Using Multimodal MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a widespread and devastating mental health disorder marked by ongoing feelings of sadness, a diminished interest in activities, and various cognitive and physical challenges. Many existing models rely exclusively on either structural MRI (sMRI) or resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) data, limiting their capacity to fully capture the complexity of brain activity and dynamics, which hampers our understanding of mental health conditions. Traditional methods often employ basic attention mechanisms that fail to grasp intricate relationships in high-dimensional neuroimaging data, leading to deficient feature representations. Furthermore, these approaches frequently overlook temporal variability, which is essential for understanding the fluctuations associated with mental health disorders. Conventional models also struggle with effective strategies for integrating information from different modalities, often lack interpretability, and tend to be computationally intensive, which limits their practical use. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel framework for detecting and classifying MDD using deep learning (DL) techniques that use both sFMRI and rs-fMRI data. Our framework employs the Dualistic-series Transformer (Dual-Trans), which features an enhanced mechanism for capturing and representing features. This includes multi-Dconv-head Temporal Attention (MDCTA) for simultaneous spectral feature extraction and Multihead Spatial Self-Attention (MSPSA) for analyzing spatial relationships within the data. Additionally, the Feature Compensation Module (FCM) assesses consistency across spatial and temporal dimensions, identifying discrepancies between modalities to enhance the model's reliability. Furthermore, the Gate Module (GM) fuses these features, enabling a decision-making process that weighs their relevance in the final representation. Ultimately, detection and classification occur in a Dualistic-series Feed-Forward Network, which processes input in parallel branches tailored for each modality while benefiting from integrated features.

articleTitle: AI and Machine Learning Applications in Hepatitis B Diagnosis: An Exploration of Techniques and Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Hepatitis B is one of the major global health challenges, affecting millions worldwide and frequently leading to serious liver conditions like hepatocellular carcinoma and cirrhosis. Early and accurate diagnosis is very important for effective management and treatment; however, most of the traditional diagnostic approaches, including serological tests, liver function tests, liver biopsy, etc., are very often affected by limitations in resource availability and diagnostic accuracy. This review paper highlights the current development in various research works on the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in the diagnosis of Hepatitis B. This paper reviews all the major ML computational techniques used in Hepatitis B diagnosis, underlining the use of various computational techniques: Generalized regression neural networks (GRNN), multilayer Mamdani fuzzy inference system (ML-MFIS), hybrid models combining clustering with ensemble learning, ANFIS, deep neural network (DNN), and support vector machine (SVM). These methodologies have been reported to show substantial improvement in the performance of diagnosis, where the maximum accuracy rate is up to 99.35%. This paper has also listed the datasets used for the studies and compared the performance metrics of these studies in terms of precision, accuracy, and F-score. Despite the progress, several issues persist, such as small dataset sizes, data imbalance, and the need for thorough validation across diverse clinical settings. Several research questions are also outlined to showcase the current ML diagnosis methods and their performances along with their limitations to provide the future research direction. It also covers the adoption of explainable AI (XAI) as of one the potential future aspect.

articleTitle: Explainable AI for Electronic Health Record (EHR) Analysis and Patient Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This work introduces a novel approach to patient risk prediction which uses a combined Logistic Regression and XGBoost for EHR analysis. The objective is to advance the performance of two models for predicting patient outcomes, like readmission to the hospital or worsening of the condition. Logistic Regression has a form of interpretability that is suitable for healthcare use, and XGBoost identifies and models complex interactions in data. The ensemble technique was developed by implementing a stacking method where the meta-learner constitutes the Logistic Regression classifier. Performance enhancement was performed by hyperparameter tuning on both models. The proposed ensemble model outperformed individual models achieving an accuracy of 93.17%. Additionally, other XAI techniques such as SHAP are utilized to provide clear and precise information to the patient based on his / her results from the model. It gives clinical professionals a consistent and easy-to-understand AI-based tool that supports improved patient care.

articleTitle: AlertCam-An Effective Anomaly Detection System using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: With the rising incidents of harassment and violence in India, particularly against women, this paper presents a real-time violence detection system using YOLO image detection models (YOLOv7, YOLOv8, and YOLOv9). The models were trained on a carefully curated and manually annotated dataset using Roboflow, ensuring robust detection across diverse scenarios. Transfer learning and hyperparameter tuning were applied to improve accuracy. The system was evaluated using key performance metrics, including mean average precision (mAP), Intersection over Union (IoU), precision, and recall, achieving 80% precision and 50–60% recall. Extensive manual testing on real-world surveillance footage and additional video sources further validated its effectiveness. Results indicate that YOLOv8 outperforms other versions in balancing speed and accuracy. This system has strong potential for deployment in law enforcement, public surveillance, and safety-critical applications.

articleTitle: Subterranean Guardian: Tunnel Safety and soil-Borne Emergency Data Transfer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Subterranean Guardian addresses the drawbacks of existing tunnel safety systems by delivering real-time monitoring and emergency response in minutes. Existing systems are frequently slow, rely on limited data, lack exact geolocation, and provide responders with delayed notifications. To address these problems, the proposed system incorporates IoT, Arduino-based sensors, GPS tracking, vibration sensors, and a soil stability monitor. These can aid in continuous data collecting and real-time alerts, as well as accurate identification of seismic events and soil instability locations, allowing for quick response to seismic occurrences and soil instability. According to the results, regular feedback improves response time (maximum 84% faster), data accuracy (98% maximum detection rate), and user satisfaction (669% maximum improvement of soil stability alerts). It is the factor that renders the system more dependable, efficient, and proactive, resulting in improved tunnel safety and reduced risks to workers and infrastructure.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Machine Learning Models and Hybrid Approaches for Fake News Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The false circulation of fake news across digital platforms has highlighted the urgent need for reliable detection systems to preserve the accuracy of information. The usefulness of different ML methods for detecting fake news is investigated and compared in this paper. We evaluated the performance of eight widely used classifiers: KNN, Naive Bayes, Random Forest Classifier, Logistic Regression, SVM, GBC, Neural Networks, and AdaBoost. The models are trained and tested on a balanced dataset using standard text preprocessing techniques. To determine which algorithm provides the most accurate classification of fake and real news, their precision, recall, F1-scores, and accuracy are evaluated. Our findings highlight the strengths and limitations of each model, offering insights into the most effective techniques for mitigating the spread of fake news. The results suggest that ensemble-based methods and deep learning approaches show significant potential in achieving higher accuracy rates, while traditional classifiers may fall short in handling complex patterns in the data.

articleTitle: An Automated IoT-Enabled Real-Time Intravenous Infusion cum Remote Patient Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in healthcare systems worldwide, including an acute shortage of nursing staff and the inability to provide continuous patient monitoring. Traditional Intravenous (IV) infusion systems, while present everywhere, have many challenges such as inconsistent flow rates and dangerous backflow issues, leading to significant risks to patient safety. These limitations amplify the burden on healthcare workers, threatening patient outcomes in high-stress environments. To address these challenges, we present an IoT-Enabled IV Infusion System with integrated remote patient monitoring capabilities. This innovative solution automates medication delivery, ensures precise flow control, and provides real-time monitoring. The system connects to a central platform via IoT, allowing healthcare providers to monitor infusion parameters remotely and receive alerts in case of anomalies, significantly reducing the need for constant bedside presence. Our implementation demonstrates enhanced safety, efficiency, and scalability. The results highlight its potential to mitigate nurse shortages, prevent medical errors, and transform IV therapy into a proactive, data-driven process. This system represents a crucial step towards resilient healthcare, ensuring patient safety and resource optimization in both routine and crisis scenarios.

articleTitle: TEC Variation Prediction through AI and Space Weather Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) require very precise Total Electron Content (TEC) variation prediction to be operating good, especially in low-latitude regions where ionospheric disturbances are more efficient. Space weather events like solar activity, geomagnetic storms, and ionospheric irregularities have powerful effect on TEC. This research proposes unique method that is AI-driven also data analysis and machine learning models are being used in various fields to predict thermal emission coefficients (TEC) variations. For improving the TEC accuracy, this approach includes data from various sources such as solar indices, geomagnetic activity, and ionospheric characteristics. Hybridmodels and various machine learning techniques are used to represent the non-linear correlations between ionospheric dynamics and space weather phenomena. The challenges that current systems face are low generalization across different geographic locations, uneven data quality, and limited prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimizing Existing SHM Systems: Retasking as a Self-Healing Solution for Improved Fault Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This paper focuses on self-healing algorithms in structural health monitoring (SHM) systems centered around the enhancement of resilience and adaptability of the systems. In this study, imports from existing methods (clustering, Fault Tolerant Multiple Redundancy (FTMR) and reinforcement learning) are analyzed against the choice of creating a novel retasking algorithm designed for dynamic resource redistribution and optimal monitoring coverage. Unlike conventional methods, retasking will allow adapting the coverage in real time, whereby system down time will be reduced, with less computational load achieved through task redistribution through functional sensors. Findings showed that retasking improved reliability and scalability of the SHM systems drastically, providing a simple yet powerful resolution towards modern infrastructure monitoring. This study stresses the retasking capability to redefine self-healing in the SHM systems for future directions in infrastructure safety.

articleTitle: Multimodal CNN-Based Framework for Enhanced Detection and Classification of Skin Cancer and Cysts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The early and precise detection and classification of skin cancers and skin cystic lesions remain extremely important in the practice of dermatology. In this paper, we present a novel multimodal CNN framework that aims to improve diagnostic performance by fusing different types of data such as dermoscopic images and histopathological slides along with clinical information and optional genomic information. The method innovatively includes several novel steps: 1. Advanced Feature Extraction Networks: Uses dedicated CNN models such as U-Net for image segmentation and ResNet for feature extraction for dermoscopy and histopathology images. 2. Innovative Feature Fusion Networks: Leverages the techniques of cross-modal attention mechanisms to integrate features from different modalities to improve the prediction performance of the model. 3. Multi-Input CNN Architecture: Processes the clinical records through its network to obtain embeddings which are fused with the image features to examine the lesion along with the patient’s data. 4. Unified Detection and Classification Model: It utilizes a multi-task learning strategy that employs attention layers for important image sections and ensemble learning to integrate forecasts from different CNN models as it does joint lesion detection with simultaneous classification. The evaluation across different datasets indicates better accuracy, sensitivity and specificity than all previous methodologies making it more applicable in real hospitals. In doing so, it tackles difficult data fusion and computation problems thus greatly improving skin cancer as well as cystic lesion detection-classification hence enhancing both clinical procedure and patient outcome.

articleTitle: Security Enhancement in MANET using Modified Crow Search Optimization Algorithm for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Mobile Ad hoc Networks (MANETs) are the integral part of advanced IoT applications, offering flexibility as well as scalability in dynamic network conditions. However, their distributed nature and reliance on wireless communication become them extremely vulnerable to security threats. This paper suggested a Modified Crow Search Optimization (MCSO) algorithm to improve the security of MANETs for IoT based applications. The recommended approach explores the intelligent foraging behavior of crows to provide secure transmission from malicious attacks. The MCSO algorithm is assessed against established methods in terms of convergence analysis. The performance of MCSO is assessed through latency as well as throughput analysis, signifying its greater efficiency over standing procedures such as SASFO, CHHSO and CSA. The latency examination discloses that MCSO reliably attains the lowest latency, fluctuating from 0.01 to 0.15, compared to larger latencies identified in CHHSO (0.03–0.16), CSA (0.03– 0.19) as well as SASFO (0.05–0.20). Furthermore, the throughput analysis shows that MCSO preserves the maximum throughput, begining at 96.7% and dropping minimally to 90.4% by the 200<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> round. These outcomes authenticate MCSO’s effectiveness in dropping latency and preserving higher throughput, thus making it a robust as well as reliable result for improving performance of a network in MANETs, mainly in IoT applications.

articleTitle: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Biomedicine and Healthcare: Improving Efficiency, Decision-Making, and Tailored Patient Care
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in biology and healthcare could change the business by boosting efficiency, decision-making, and patient care. AI technologies including machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing are being used in healthcare diagnosis, treatment, drug discovery, and administration. As AI analyzes enormous amounts of complicated medical data, finds patterns, and predicts, diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making have increased, enabling early identification of cancer, cardiovascular, and neurological diseases. In addition to diagnostic applications, AI-driven systems are improving predictive analytics, helping healthcare providers forecast patient outcomes, optimize treatment plans, and reduce medical errors. Another area where AI is helping is personalized medicine and tailored patient care. AI systems analyze genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors to design treatment regimens, increasing patient results and lowering side effects. AI applications in drug research and development have also sped the discovery of new medicinal compounds and optimized clinical trial designs for better results and faster approval. AI in healthcare faces data privacy problems, regulatory difficulties, and the requirement for robeust training datasets to maintain system accuracy, despite significant gains. AI decision-making in medicine requires careful ethical concerns, notably transparency and accountability. AI technology integration into healthcare systems will improve patient experiences, results, efficiency, cost, and equity. This study examines AI's uses in biomedicine and healthcare, including successes, problems, and future directions.

articleTitle: CAMICS: A Context-Aware Multi-Intent Conversational System for Enhanced AI-Driven Customer Interaction Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Customer interaction models are rapidly evolving with the advent of AI-driven chatbots and virtual assistants, yet challenges remain in achieving contextually aware, efficient, and scalable systems. This paper presents the Context-Aware Multi-Intent Conversational System (CAMICS), a novel architecture that integrates context encoding, multi-task learning, and efficient response generation to transform customer service interactions. Leveraging the Customer Support on Twitter dataset, CAMICS performs better state-of-the-art models across multiple tasks. For intent classification, CAMICS achieves an F1-score of 94.5%, surpassing BERT (91.0%) and CNN-based approaches (86.8%). In sentiment analysis, it obtains a macro F1-score of 92.1%, significantly outperforming logistic regression (77.5%) and Random Forest models (80.7%). The response generation module achieves BLEU and ROUGE-L scores of 56.7% and 54.9%, respectively, demonstrating its capability to generate high-quality, contextually relevant responses compared to GPT-2 (51.4% BLEU, 49.3% ROUGE-L). The CAMICS model also exhibits computational efficiency, with an inference time of 11.5 ms per conversation and reduced GPU memory usage (490 MB), making it suitable for real-time applications. An ablation study further highlights the critical contributions of the context encoder and multi-task learning modules to the overall performance.

articleTitle: Butterfly Optimization and Deep Learning to Classify Heart Sound Signal
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Heart sound signals, or PCG recordings, provide a valuable non-invasive alternative to traditional diagnostic methods like CXR and blood tests for detecting cardiovascular disease. In this study, PCG data are collected, and features such as MFCC and WST are extracted to capture both time and frequency information. These features are used to classify the signals into normal and abnormal categories using DL models, including CNN, Bi-LSTM, and Bi-RNN. The study conducts extensive experiments using individual and combined features, showing that combining features enhances classification accuracy. The proposed CNN model, optimized with the Butterfly Optimization Algorithm, achieves an impressive classification accuracy of 99.07%, outperforming other models. This result highlights the effectiveness of using PCG signals and advanced DL techniques for accurate cardiovascular disease detection, offering a noninvasive and efficient alternative for early diagnosis.

articleTitle: Image Compression and Enhancement Using Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: These days, applications like transmission and database storage require image compression. This essay examines and discusses picture compression, the need for compression, basic tenets, classifications of compression, and different algorithms a compression of images. This essay aims to provide a guide for choose one of the widely used image compression techniques constructed using Wavelet, JPEG/DCT, VQ, and fractal methods. We examine and debate the benefits and drawbacks of these techniques for grayscale picture compression provide an experimental comparison using a common image size of 256 x 25. Many highly tuned applications, like geophysics, navigation, nondestructive testing, and medical imaging, which demand precise recoveries of original pictures, require lossless compression. Deep learning-based techniques have increasingly been used in image compression with numerous encouraging outcomes. For addressing the traditional as well as the current issues of image compression, in this work lite module based neural network is proposed. Further, the performance of the algorithm is optimized using the slime mold optimization technique. The performance of the proposed method is compared with the traditional methods of image compression such as CNN and SVM in terms of PSNR, MSE, and SSIM metrics.

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving Healthcare Based on Secure Mathematical Foundations of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The swift development of digital technology in the healthcare industry has made it crucial to protect sensitive patient data while maintaining its usefulness. One such technique is Homomorphic Encryption (HE), a powerful paradigm that enables computations on encrypted data without the requirement for decryption. This feature ensures that confidential health information remains secure while still allowing for complex analyses and operations. There are three primary categories of HE includes Partially Homomorphic Encryption (PHE), Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption (SHE) and Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE). The experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of HE. In particular, FHE provides the most extensive capabilities by permitting an infinite amount of addition and multiplication operations on ciphertexts. Similarly, FHE ensures semantic security and correctness over other HE techniques based on proper parameter optimization through squashing and bootstrapping. Bootstrapping maintains the noise within safe limit whereas squashing reduces decryption complexity.The performance analysis proves that RLWE based FHE ensures both privacy and utility for healthcare data in computationally efficient way. The privacy-preserving nature of FHE along with its ability to support complex computations and its strong mathematical foundation proving its potential for real-world use cases like secure cloud computing, privacy-preserving machine learning and secure data analytics in healthcare etc.

articleTitle: Harnessing AI and Machine Learning to Transform English Language Learning Experiences
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This study presents a methodology for evaluating argumentative essays from English language learners (ELLs) in grades 8 through 12, utilizing the ELLIPSE corpus. The essays are assessed across six critical metrics: coherence, syntax, vocabulary, phraseology, grammar, and conventions, with ratings from 1.0 to 5.0. The process begins with data collection, followed by preprocessing steps to prepare the text for machine learning. This includes removing punctuation, stopwords, stemming, lemmatization, and expanding contractions to enhance text quality for analysis. Advanced feature extraction techniques are then applied, utilizing word embeddings to convert textual data into dense vector representations. These embeddings capture the syntactic and semantic nuances of the text, making it suitable for machine learning models. The vectorized data is input into Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which are adept at handling sequential data. LSTMs manage information flow through cell states and gates, allowing them to capture long-term dependencies in the text effectively. The LSTM network processes the text sequentially, leveraging previous words to make informed classification decisions. The resulting model provides high-accuracy classifications of essays based on the six metrics, offering insights into learners' proficiency levels. This methodology demonstrates a robust application of AI and machine learning in enhancing English language learning, with potential uses in personalized education and automated assessment systems. The study highlights the effectiveness of integrating advanced feature extraction and sequential modeling techniques to assess and improve language proficiency among students. The proposed Word Embedding-based LSTM Model, however, gave out a great result where it produced an accuracy of 98% and it is implemented in python.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Networks for Advanced Medication Security in IoT-Enabled Smart Robotic Dispensing Cabinets
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Ensuring advanced medication security is of the utmost importance in smart robotic dispensing cabinets enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT). Strong pharmaceutical security is of the utmost importance in smart robotic dispensing cabinets that the IoT enables. To strengthen security measures in these systems, this research presents a new method that uses deep neural networks (DNNs). The proposed system improves the identification of potential medication mistakes and unauthorized access by using DNNs' anomaly detection and pattern recognition capabilities. A thorough security layer is created by incorporating DNN models into the IoT design of smart cabinets to address drug administration and dispensation weaknesses. Discovering security breaches or procedural problems entails training DNNs on large datasets to detect typical operating patterns and abnormalities. It shows that the strategy significantly improves security procedures and operational dependability in real-world conditions via simulations and validation experiments, proving its usefulness. Providing a strong answer to the problems of improving the effectiveness of drug administration in healthcare settings based on the IoT helps move healthcare technology forward. The technology improves pharmaceutical security and lays the groundwork for responsive and adaptable healthcare infrastructures. This study will make improving the dependability and safety of healthcare delivery systems possible.

articleTitle: Phishing Detection and Response System with XGBOOST Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Email phishing attacks are one of the most severe threats to personal, organizational, and financial information through email and websites. The attackers exploit human vulnerabilities to extract confidential information from users. The proposed system utilizes an AI-based algorithm, XGBoost, which is well known for its efficiency in building a robust machine learning model with high classification accuracy. It uses gradient boosting to handle large datasets with precision, ensuring reliable detection of fraudulent communications. The system is trained on a diversified dataset containing both phishing and legitimate emails and web pages. Key feature elements include URL extraction, email headers, message content, and domain information. Initially, the system preprocesses the collected data by extracting relevant features and converting them to a machine-readable format for training. An XGBoost model then has to be fitted to labeled data that can identify phishing attempts through subtle anomalies. The system then goes live, operating in real-time, and scans incoming emails and web pages and instantly alerts users of phishing attempts it detects on them. Such a system minimizes by many folds the success of phishing attack intentions. Self-updating systems through new data releases on phishing ensure an adaptable approach to active threats. This also improves online cybersecurity through the scalable and efficient detection of phishing attacks. This system has a sufficient amount of machine learning usage which is effective for the identification of differences between legitimate and malicious contents, which contributes to this proposed solution being a safer digital space. Real-time alert feature integration in this system makes it more protective for the user since it detects any potential threats beforehand. Also, this proposed solution has an adaptive and scalable nature that changes with time according to new phishing strategies evolved in various contexts. It reduces the chances of phishing attacks on users and thus increases overall cybersecurity with reduced impacts of phishing scams.

articleTitle: Advancing Drone-Based Traffic Surveillance: A Review and Novel Framework for Attention-Guided Motion Deblurring and Compensation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This paper investigates the critical challenges of motion deblurring and compensation in drone-based traffic surveillance, focusing on the transformative potential of Attention-Guided Deblurring Transformer (AGDT). The framework employs self-attention mechanisms to address non-uniform blur and integrates hybrid motion compensation techniques for stabilizing dynamic video feeds. Quantitative evaluation using metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and MOTA demonstrates AGDT's remarkable ability to enhance video clarity, ensure smooth frame transitions, and improve multi-object tracking accuracy under real-time constraints. The study also provides a comparative analysis of state-of-the-art methods, highlighting AGDT's superior performance while identifying areas for future optimization.

articleTitle: Spatial-Scale Sensitivity in SEBAL Evapotranspiration Estimation for Crop Health Monitoring with Sentinel-2A
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The objective of this study is to apply Sentinel-2 satellite data for the monitoring of evapotranspiration of various crop cycles in Sillod, Maharashtra, India, including cotton, sugarcane, wheat, and maize. It uses a combination of some ET estimation methods, such as simplified ET and Priestley-Taylor methods, with net radiation (Rn) and sensible heat flux (H) calculations to estimate water extraction for each crop at four different times in June 2023 to February 2024. Some trends noticed here are that Rn was pretty consistent and high with fluctuating H values depending on the crop type or the growth stage. The minimum ET map values with the simple approach showed low minimum values for all study periods suggesting extensive water loss to ET processes. Spatial ET map variabilities were noticed with the Priestley-Taylor method, where it exhibited red and yellow color palettes that consider different crop water demands. To verify Sentinel-2-derived ET estimates, benchmarking using ERA5 evapotranspiration was calculated. The average ERA5 evaporation value from vegetation transpiration amounts to 1.21×10–10 in units of m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/s, which compares well with the mean obtained from NDVI on Sentinel-2 equaling 0.1636. This cross-validation test makes sure our estimates of ET by Sentinel-2 are compatible with global datasets, which further supports the reliability and accuracy of the results derived. This study demonstrated strong effectiveness of a technique combining satellite-based ET estimation with remote sensing for the support of precision agriculture and sustainable water management. The findings are well-suited to provide valuable insights into optimizing crop water use in semi-arid regions, focusing on the potential of remote sensing for improving agricultural monitoring and resource planning.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Security in MANET using Modified Crow Harris Hawks Optimization Algorithm for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Mobile Ad hoc Networks (MANETs) are dynamic and decentralized wireless networks that play a essential role in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. MANET is a frequently used independent wireless architecture to communicate with mobile nodes. Instead, MANET operates without a central hub, which might be useful in certain situations: emergent activities, defense-related applications, electronic gadgets, and resident services. So many people utilize MANET for their facilities, it is important to ensure that only authorized users may connect to the network. However, their inherent characteristics, such as dynamic topology, limited resources, and lack of centralized control, expose them to various security vulnerabilities. This paper presents a new approach for enhancing network security in MANETs using the Modified Crow Harris Hawks Optimization (MCHO) algorithm. The proposed MCHO algorithm joins the exploration strengths of the Crow Search Algorithm and the exploitative capabilities of Harris Hawks Optimization, attaining a robust stability among convergence speed as well as solution quality. Extensive simulations were conducted to evaluate the algorithm's performance under different MANET scenarios, comparing it with existing methods such as Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The results demonstrate the performance of optimization algorithms—ACO, GA, CHHSO as well as MCHO—assessed in terms of their cost function over improving iterations. The analysis shows that MCHO always outperforms the remaining algorithms, achieving the highest cost function of 0.23 at 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> iteration, followed by CHHSO with a cost function of 0.20. GA attains a reasonable progress with a cost function of 0.19, while ACO shows the least performance, achieving only 0.16 at the same point. These results highlight the superiority of MCHO in enhancing the security for the allocated scenario.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Custom Neural Network Model and VGG-16 for Multi-class Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This study assesses the performance of CustomNet, a lightweight neural network model trained using NumPy and Pandas, compared to the VGG-16 architecture on the datasets of MNIST, Fashion MNIST, and Virus MNIST. With fewer parameters, CustomNet achieves competitive accuracy since it is designed for reduced computational complexity. Model performance was assessed using metrics such F1 score, accuracy, precision, and recall. CustomNet provides a compelling trade-off between computational efficiency and accuracy, making it appropriate for resource-constrained contexts, even if the VGG-16 model showed better accuracy.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Understanding Animal Behavior Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Animals need health and wellbeing monitoring. It requires constant care, and observation. Manual tracking involves humans visually observing and recording animal movements which makes data management difficult and time-consuming. This automated animal behavior tracking system uses machine learning to accurately observe and comprehend animal behavior. The suggested study uses VGG-16 and ResNet50 for animal identification and LRCN for behavior detection. ResNet50 and VGG-16 process camera tape data. ResNet50 outperforms VGG-16 in cat and dog identification. The LRCN model helps identify animal behavior accurately. The UCF-50 dataset was first created to predict general human behavior, but it did not specifically reflect the actions of cats and dogs, which limited its application to these animals. In order to close this gap and make sure the LRCN model could successfully adapt to cats and dogs, for this study, a customized dataset centered on their distinctive behavioral pattern was exclusively created. The problem of reducing false positives in behavior detection is also addressed by the hybrid strategy that combines LRCN with ResNet50, producing predictions that are more accurate and trustworthy. Proactive health and behavior monitoring is encouraged by this integration, which improves the system's capacity to recognize, detect, and forecast animal behaviors.

articleTitle: Automated Bridge Inspection and Structural Damage Detection Using YOLOv5-s
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: An effective structural health monitoring system ensures that bridge structures are safe and durable. This paper introduces an innovative approach toward the automation of bridge inspection and the detection of structural damage using object detection with the YOLOv5-s algorithm. The model optimizes various types of structural defects such as cracks, corrosion, spalling, and deformation from image data. Based on high-speed performance and accuracy, the YOLOv5-s model is suited to handle larger datasets and will thus provide continuous, real-time monitoring of bridge conditions. With the model trained and tested on a very extensive dataset of bridge images, we show that it guarantees high accuracy in both defect detection and localization for this work. Our results suggest that an automated solution might save effort and reduce more time spent in the effort to achieve manual inspections. Future work involves improving the robustness of the model with regard to varied environments and adding more structural components.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Risk Stratification in Rural Healthcare During the Pandemic: An Ensemble Voting Classifier Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This research presents an Ensemble Voting Classifier that is aimed at enhancing the accessibility of healthcare in rural areas during the pandemic. The model applies a range of machine learning algorithms to make timely interventions and classify patients according to their risk levels. It was evaluated with an impressive AUC-ROC of 98.64% and an accuracy of 97.58% on a comprehensive dataset. These indicators are shown to be able to detect patients at a greater risk of poor health outcomes when the resources are scarcer, an important component in reducing health disparities. Ensemble learning methodologies may be helpful in the decision-making of rural health care since the approach developed in this paper exceeds the state of the art. The study results indicate the promise of applying machine learning to enhance healthcare outcomes and optimize triaging patients in case of public health emergencies, hence more equal access to care for vulnerable populations.

articleTitle: Secure Bitcoin Hardware Wallet Design, Implementation, and Security Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This paper presents a Cryptocurrency security presents significant challenges in safeguarding digital assets against evolving threats. This paper introduces a secure, open-source Bitcoin hardware wallet emphasizing affordability, transparency, and user empowerment. Unlike proprietary commercial solutions, the proposed wallet leverages an air-gapped design using the Raspberry Pi Zero to isolate cryptographic operations from network-based vulnerabilities. Integrating a user-friendly LCD interface and QR code capabilities, the wallet ensures intuitive operation and robust security. The paper implements advanced cryptographic techniques for key management, achieving a functional prototype supporting multiple cryptocurrencies. By adopting a transparent, modular design, this research contributes to the broader discourse on decentralized asset security and encourages innovation within the cryptocurrency ecosystem. This wallet demonstrates a paradigm shift in accessible, secure digital asset management and underscores the significance of open-source solutions in the blockchain era.

articleTitle: Enhanced Framework for Predictive Analytics of Infants in Neonatal Integrating AI & IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs) play a significant role in saving the lives of high-risk infants. However, conventional monitoring systems primarily focus on real-time tracking without integrating predictive analytics, leading to delays in identifying potentially life-threatening conditions such as jaundice, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, hydrocephalus, microcephaly, or respiratory failure. The proposed novel framework addresses the gap identified above by using noninvasive Internet of Things (IoT)-)-enabled devices with advanced machine learning models to monitor critical health metrics—such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, and body temperature—in real-time. The proposed architecture uses a hybrid Artificial Intelligence (AI) approach by combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Gradient Boosting techniques, particularly XGBoost, to improve prediction performance and get around overfitting. This approach proactively detects possible health hazards by utilizing IoT sensor data. Compared to the existing techniques, the proposed model performs better, with an accuracy of 95.89% when tested on a dataset of neonatal conditions. The high efficiency of the proposed system offers promising potential for early diagnosis of neonatal conditions and improved health outcomes through intervention before serious complications arise. Neonatal care is handled proactively rather than reactively in this prototypical attempt toward innovative, technology-oriented health systems. Future works will focus on handling data privacy issues and scaling the dataset to optimize model interpretability in IoT-based healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Brain Tumors in CT Images: A Comparative Analysis Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Techniques and Support Vector Machine (SVM)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Brain tumor segmentation using CT scans is essential for diagnosis, therapy planning, and progression tracking. This study compares SVM and CNN methods for segmenting brain tumors in CT images. These methods will be assessed for tumor boundary accuracy. To assure uniformity and quality, this study employed preprocessed CT scans from brain tumor patients. CNN uses deep learning to automatically learn hierarchical features during training, while SVM uses handcrafted image features. SVM uses texture analysis, intensity thresholding, and shape descriptors to train the classifier to discriminate tumor and non-tumor regions. The CNN model learns features directly from raw pixel data, using deep convolutional layers' hierarchical nature to capture complex patterns and spatial correlations in images. Both models are split-sampled, trained, validated, and assessed for robustness and generalizability. Performance indicators including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and Dice similarity coefficient quantify segmentation results. To examine segmentation results' clinical relevance, professional radiologists do qualitative assessments. Deep learning techniques can be used in medical image analysis, since the CNN model surpasses the SVM model in segmentation accuracy and resilience. SVM has lesser performance but better computing economy and interpretability, which may be useful in some therapeutic scenarios. This work sheds light on the pros and cons of SVM and CNN methods for brain tumor segmentation in CT images, helping physicians create more accurate and efficient tools. CNNs are excellent tools for this endeavor, but classical machine learning methods have a place, especially in cases where computational resources are restricted or model interpretability is important.

articleTitle: Advancing Carbon Emission Prediction through Machine Learning: The Impact of Fossil, Nuclear, and Renewable Energies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Accurate prediction of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions is significant in the development of appropriate strategies to mitigate climate change. This study applies machine learning methodologies for the forecast of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions using a global dataset from I960 to 2022. The dataset used from Kaggle comprises all the relevant features: power output from fossil fuels, nuclear, and renewables, in addition to GDP and land area. Three machine learning models were constructed and evaluated for their effectiveness in prediction: Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Linear Regression. The Random Forest model had the highest accuracy, as demonstrated by its R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.995, which showcases its strength in handling intricate, nonlinear interactions and identifying key variables, such as dependence on fossil fuels. The R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score for Gradient Boosting was 0.987, which shows that this model is similarly good at identifying complex relationships between features. Conversely, Linear Regression underperformed despite its processing efficiency due to its constraints with nonlinear data. This study highlights the efficacy of ensemble models in predicting CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. It offers practical recommendations for policymakers to formulate strategies to decrease fossil fuel use and promote renewable energy utilization. Future endeavors will include real-time data and investigate hybrid models to enhance temporal forecasting and practical application.

articleTitle: Hybrid Unified AI-Based Biometric Authentication: A Low-Power, High-Security Scheme
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Biometric options integrated with the surpassing conventional locks for the expedient advancement of smart home technology has revolutionized home security. The Hybrid Unified Multimodal Biometric Integration Algorithm (HUMBIA), is proposed in this paper, with integrated modules like voice, facial, and fingerprint recognition to progress admittance control. The proposed HUMBIA algorithm reduces False Acceptance Rates (FAR) and False Rejection Rates (FRR) by incorporating robust refuge scheme with enhanced accurateness through the use of the ESP32 microcontroller and an amalgamation of biometric sense modality. The reliable performance in a variety of scenarios is analysed to ensure the scheme's dynamic adaptation by changing ecological environments. The evaluation with recent current techniques demonstrates the better precision and sensitivity of HUMBIA's authentication. Contemporary hardware integrated with AI driven processes is suggested in the proposed system for advanced security and user expediency. This research can mark a significant and trending progression in smart home-based security scheme.

articleTitle: A Secure Digital Twin Healthcare Framework for Precision Medicine: Integrating IoMT, ML and Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Digital Twin is a virtual replica of a physical system that uses real-time sensor data along with historical data to predict and simulate behaviors. In healthcare, the Digital Patient Twin represents a complete virtual copy of an individual’s medical records updated in real-time with data from tests and sensors embedded in wearable devices. Integrated care offered by traditional healthcare systems encounters a challenge in providing real-time monitoring due to the lack of interoperability between IoT devices and electronic health record (EHR) systems. Machine learning (ML)-based predictive modeling facilitates timely interventions and personalized treatment strategies, which have been shown to improve patient outcomes. Fog computing enhances the speed of data processing, which is based on IoT, but also poses many security issues in the following ways: This project investigates how Digital Twin technology can solve these challenges through the power of real-time monitoring, providing personalized care while enhancing IoT-connected healthcare security. Along with this, it also works on advanced predictive time series analytics, virtual scenarios for the optimization of IoT sensor networks, securing patient data against threats, etc. The project also integrates the use of cloud and fog infrastructures to facilitate scalable data storage, high availability, and rapid processing of data for real-time insights and decision-making.

articleTitle: Graph-Based Deep Learning Models for Optimized Routing in Autonomous Networks Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The complexity of modern networks is increasing, and new sophisticated routing methods are needed in the face of dynamic situations. Traditional routing algorithms are highly used, but they are subjected to limitations in handling real-time changes and scalability in a large complex network. Such techniques tend to fail in finding an optimal latency, throughput, and packet delivery ratio in dynamic environments where conditions change over time. This study proposes a new methodology known as GNN-RL, or Graph Neural Networks combined with Reinforcement Learning, to overcome traditional shortfalls by applying the graph-based structure of networks and adaptive decision-making capabilities of RL in dynamically modifying routing decisions, thus optimizing network performance in real time. Experimental results show that GNN-RL outperformed the traditional algorithms: achieving superior throughput (40%), latency (25%), and packet delivery ratio (20%). It resulted in a 90% improvement in overall performance when compared to Dijkstra's Algorithm, AODV, and OSPF at 80%, 80%, and 75%, respectively. The model is well set to adapt and optimize its routing decisions in real-time environments; it is promising for autonomous management of future networks. Results confirm that GNN-RL could offer improved routing strategies with the power to be efficient, scalable, and robust in comparison to traditional routing techniques.

articleTitle: Efficient Source-Level Waste Segregation Using CNN-Based Waste Classifier with IoT-Enabled Smart Bins and Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Image processing and deep learning techniques have demonstrated their efficacy as valuable tools for classifying municipal solid waste. This study presents a comparative review of the recent advancement in waste classification techniques and their significance. Further, an attempt has been made to prepare a reliable dataset by integrating datasets from the public domain and web images. Architectures consisting of pre-trained models, namely Inception V3, ResNet, VGG19, DenseNet, and Xception, based on Convolution Neural Networks, were considered. In that process, it was observed that models Inception V3 and Xception were performing exceptionally well. Further, both the models were fine-tuned through hyperparameter tuning, and Inception V3 and Xception yielded 93% and 94.4% accuracy, respectively. The identified best model was further deployed on the mobile app for waste classification, and the advanced bin monitoring unit (ABMU) was developed for smart bins to facilitate source-level segregation of waste. Both these systems will guide the user in the scientific disposal of waste and improve people's awareness of efficient disposal practices according to prevailing guidelines.

articleTitle: BoTNetShield: Intelligent IoT Security Framework using Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The "Internet of Things (IoT)" sector has grown in recent years, penetrating many different markets. The diversity and diminutive size of Internet-connected gadgets render them vulnerable to attacks. Improving and managing network forensic processes to avoid the various attacks, key logging, and denial of service becomes challenging in big and heterogeneous networks. Implementing high-end safety systems is challenging in IoT networks due to their variety and resource restrictions. Using deep learning, botnet detection is made better. It often requires a great deal of internet engagement. Internet of Things devices with little RAM have difficulties when using deep learning. This study use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for model training and Similarity Associated Feature Selection (SAFS) to decrease the dimensionality of smaller Internet of Things (IoT) traffic networks in order to effectively classify attacks in devices with limited memory. The effectiveness of botnet attacks is evaluated by first collecting datasets from the internet. By improving attack detection data from acquired datasets, data cleaning aids in eliminating unnecessary information. To enhance attack detection, SAFS cleans the data and then extracts efficient deep features. To classify risks to Internet of Things devices based on retrieved deep data, an efficient Recurrent Neural Network method is employed. Research evaluations compare proposed methods against existing ones in order to determine whether one is more effective.

articleTitle: Combining Speech Recognition and Machine Learning for Context-Aware English Pronunciation Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The use of pronunciation assessment is vital for the improvement of the aspect of English language for learners learning it like foreigners. The existing approaches are based upon the conceptual representations and the scoring functions which necessarily focus on simple comparison, and typically fail to offer adaptive feedback in response to contextual changes.
