Current methods for building up LSTM models fail to address the complex relationship between phonemes and the patterns in which they appear, thus producing inaccurate evaluations. This research work therefore recommended the usage of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-Lstm) networks and an Attention Mechanism, for enhancing the first approach’s precision and readability of the pronunciation evaluation. In the Bi-Lstm network, considered forward phonetic sequences and backward phonetic sequences so that temporal dependencies are also learned, and the AM forced the model to pay more attention to any mispronunciation occurrence. The proposed system takes advantage of speech recognition to get the phonetic features, and uses the Bi-Lstm-Attention model to give the quality of pronunciation scores. Native vs nonnative English speakers experimentations show positive results the proposed model achieves better accuracy coupled with better error detecting capability than the LSTM Based models. This context-aware framework gives detailed, accurate, real-time commentary, and it is a very useful tool which language learners as well as educators can use to pretty precisely determine error-ridden or better: error-free pronunciation patterns.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Neural Network-based Bone Marrow Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Precise delineation and safeguarding of the functional bone marrow (FBM) in the process of radiotherapy planning have the potential to mitigate pelvic hematological toxicity. Radiotherapy is the primary therapeutic option for numerous pelvic cancers; however, there is a possibility that high-intensity radiation might cause harm to the FBM. The traditional approach to delineate the FBM is both time-intensive and demanding in terms of labour, making an efficient and precise bone marrow identification a valuable asset in clinical settings. Graph convolutional neural networks (GNNs) have gained popularity for semi-supervised classification, particularly in bone marrow image analysis. Prior GNN-based approaches primarily utilized a single graph neural network or graph filter to extract bone marrow characteristics, failing to exploit the potential of GNNs. Classical GNNs also face issues of oversmoothing. To address these limitations, we propose a hybrid method, the GNN-GS combination, which leverages both GNN and GraphSAGE. By employing performance criteria such as accuracy (ACC), precision (PRE), and the F1-score, we conducted a comparative evaluation of our suggested technique against other methods deemed to be as advanced as possible. The outcomes reveal a notable enhancement in ACC, PRE, and F1-score by 2.32%, 6.47%, and 2.75%, respectively, for the specified dataset. These comparative results establish the suitability of our proposed method for addressing bone marrow classification challenges.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Poultry Diseases Using Deep Learning and Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Early, accurate detection of chicken diseases is necessary for promoting sustainable farming techniques, enhancing poultry health, and lowering of economic losses. This paper presents a deep learning-based method using transfer learning with the EfficientNetB5 architecture to classify chicken health issues into four categories: healthy, Disease A, Disease B, and Disease C using photo data. Using a powerful training pipeline and thorough evaluation, the model not only achieved remarkable overall accuracy of 97% by surpassing 93% across all classes but also high precision, recall, and F1-scores. Closely inspection hhhkof the confusion matrix and classification metrics confirmed that the method could effectively separate visually similar but complex disease kinds. Analyzing the deployment alternatives of this model also addressed concerns such hardware constraints, scalability, and the need of real-time inference to enable useful use in chicken farms. This work presents a noninvasive, efficient diagnostic method to help early intervention and disease control in chicken production as well as showing how well advanced convolutional neural networks address significant agricultural challenges. The findings of this study suggest to a transformational route towards adding AI-driven solutions in agriculture, therefore guaranteeing better animal welfare, more farm productivity, and a sustainable future for chicken health management.

articleTitle: Advancing Personalized Medicine Using Genomic Data Analysis and Predictive Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Personalized medicine is changing because it allows for more personalized treatment plans thanks to the combination of genetic data analysis and prediction models. This study uses large genetic datasets to create and test predictive models that find how each person will respond to treatment. Along with more standard statistical methods like regression analysis, we used a number of different computer techniques, such as machine learning tools like Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, and Neural Networks. As part of our method, we preprocessed genetic data, chose features to find important variables, and trained the model using a split-sample validation method to make sure it was reliable. The models were judged on how well they could predict treatment results based on their accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Key results show that ensemble methods, especially Random Forests, work better than single methods because they can handle the complex and high-dimensional nature of genetic data better. Our best model was able to guess 89% of the time, which shows that it has a lot of promise to make professional decision-making better. This model worked very well with a variety of genetic datasets, which made it even more useful for a wide range of patient groups. Our study shows how useful it is to use advanced machine learning methods along with genetic data to make personalized medicine better. Precision medicine promises to change the way healthcare is provided by making diagnoses more accurate, treatment plans more effective, and results better. More study and use of these models could lead to wide use in hospital settings, which would improve care for patients around the world.

articleTitle: Sustainable Water Management in Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This paper uses machine learning models to optimize the utilization of water in precision agriculture. The main objective is to create a dependable system that can forecast the ideal irrigation conditions, increasing sustainability and efficiency. The process entails the thoughtful placement of sensors, the creation of a wireless network of sensors (WSN), as well as the examination of a carefully selected dataset that includes vital variables like humidity, temperature, precipitation, wind speed, along with soil moisture. The dataset's integrity is guaranteed by further data pre-processing, which includes operations like cleaning, feature significance analysis, and refining. The 105,217-entry dataset provides the basis for training and assessing machine learning models, including Random Forest, the Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machines (SVM), along with Neural Network. The findings show that the Random Forest model performs better than the other models, with an astounding accuracy of 92.68%. At 91.83% accuracy, the model based on Decision Trees comes a close second. With accuracy levels of 90.78% & 90.21%, respectively, SVM as well as Neural Network models perform competitively. The Random Forest model's accuracy in forecasting ideal irrigation conditions is further supported by the precision along with F1-Score measures. This paper provides a strong foundation for environmentally friendly water use and offers insightful information about using machine learning techniques for precision agriculture.

Index Terms: Accuracy Of The Random Forest Model

articleTitle: A Web-Based System for QR Code Flag Identification and DecodingWith Python and Flask
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The flag-identifying tool based on QR codes here is fresh and made exclusively for a Kali Linux environment, developed in Flask for the Web. Most of them are the traditional or default QR code scanners, it's a complete zbarimg-tool, which is available as a native tool in many Linux Flavors, so it is most compatible and performs better in a Kali setup as compared to its counterparts. The tool simply does QR code reading from a very particular local machine folder along a very organized, systematic approach in handling images. Users will upload images containing QR codes over a web interface, while app.py works to process the images, decode the data, and ultimately reveal Capture The Flag (CTF) lying within the images. Indeed, only the relevant flags would return, thus saving on the user time during a CTF or cybersecurity training session. Taking advantage of native command-line utilities makes the project an offering that is indeed innovative and a first in the field of QR-code flag output extraction. This organized structure affords the tool orderly file storage and processing, a strong and scalable solution to a lover of cybersecurity and a professional. Well, this QR flag decoder is up and coming, as it emphasizes simplicity, accuracy, and using Linux-native utilities-a really big leap forward in automated QR decoding for CTF challenges and beyond.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Prognostics for Genetic Disorder Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: By improving the precision of genetic abnormality diagnosis and prediction, machine learning is transforming healthcare and creating opportunities for personalized treatments and early intervention. This research explores the application of machine learning methodologies in the analysis of patient medical records and large genomic datasets for genetic disease prediction. The technology correctly diagnoses hereditary disorders such as Huntington’s disease, muscular dystrophy, and cystic fibrosis through complex approaches such as neural networks, decision trees, and support vector machines. By integrating crucial elements such as genetic mutations, family medical history, and environmental factors, the framework efficiently evaluates possible genetic hazards. This creative approach facilitates the implementation of individualized treatments and preventive healthcare measures, which reduces the load on medical resources while improving patient care. The project highlights how revolutionary data-driven.

articleTitle: A Sophisticated Framework Designed for Deepfake Detection Using CNN and LSTM for Enhanced Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Digital literacy is changing very fast, and deepfakes in the context of video call for an important challenge. This study put forward a new approach that combines the strengths of DenseNet v2, LSTM, and MLP architectures to enhance the design of a multi-modal framework for the detection of deepfake videos. We manage an exhaustive survey on deep fake detection that discusses crucial characteristics and techniques needed. This proposed model integrates the benefits of LSTM networks and MLP classifiers with the point birth functionalities of DenseNet v2, thereby forming a robust and efficient framework. The training process involves fine-tuning key parameters so that the model is accurate, and we describe some of the tools we used to preprocess the data and evaluate the models. This work provides a comprehensive performance analysis of the proposed experimental results using precision-recall curves, confusion matrix heatmaps, F1 score comparison bar charts, and delicacy box plots. The proposed multi-modal approach has shown to be better in discovering against the compared models, and thus, is promising for practical usage. This work contributes to both the field of deepfake detection and the wider debate on machine literacy at the intersection with video analysis using CNN algorithm.

articleTitle: COP-Detect: An End-to-End Transformer based Enhanced Colon Polyp Detection and Segmentation Framework Using Colonoscopy Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Detecting polyps poses a significant challenge for the automated study of endoscopic images in computer-assisted clinical support systems.Our proposed deep learning approach, COP-Detect, addresses these issues through a series of advanced techniques. We start by preprocessing colonoscopy images using essential steps such as resizing, normalization, and data augmentation techniques, including geometric transformations and photometric adjustments.Dual-Group Feature Amplification Transformer (DG-Trans) this component enhances feature extraction by providing dual-adjust feature enrichment and group-wise feature enhancement, capturing both shallow and deep features critical for effective segmentation. Group-wise enhancement improves feature extraction within specific channels.In the decoder path, the Refined-Up Sampling Module (R-UP) restores detailed information in the segmentation maps, while the Adaptive Receptive-Field Detection Layer (ARD) uses atrous convolutions to capture contextual details surrounding polyps. Finally, the Deep Supervision Spatial Segmentation Layer (D3SL) includes auxiliary segmentation heads at various stages, predicting segmentation maps alongside the main output to enhance overall model performance.

articleTitle: Industrial Internet of Things Energy Efficiency: Investigating Low-Power Communication Protocols and Eco-Friendly Data Management in Manufacturing Settings
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: A revolutionary change in production processes, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) allows for the acquisition and analysis of data in real-time, which in turn improves operational efficiency. But there are serious worries about energy consumption and environmental effect due to the expansion of IIoT devices. In order to improve energy efficiency in manufacturing environments, this research explores low-power communication protocols and eco-friendly data management systems. Our evaluation is based on a thorough examination of existing low-power communication protocols, including LoRaWAN, Zigbee, and NB-IoT, and how well they reduce power consumption without compromising device connectivity. To further lessen the environmental impact of data processing and transmission, we investigate green data management strategies such as data aggregation and edge computing. The study uses a multi-pronged strategy, combining theoretical research with practical case studies, to measure the potential energy savings that can be achieved by applying these protocols and management techniques. The findings support the idea that a more eco-friendly production ecosystem can be achieved by reducing energy usage significantly through the optimization of communication protocols in conjunction with the adoption of sustainable data management procedures. In order to fully harness the energy-saving potential of IIoT, we also bring attention to the problems with current low-power protocols, including their inability to scale and their lack of compatibility. This research seeks to lay the groundwork for a future where IIoT is more sustainable through the use of cutting-edge communication technologies and creative data management strategies. Its ultimate goal is to contribute to the larger objectives of Industry 4.0 and environmental responsibility.

articleTitle: Optimizing Financial Security with Cloud AI: Implementing Deep Q-Network and Transfer Learning for Risk Management and Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Fraud detection and risk management remain to be significant issues in financial security due to constantly changing threats. This research introduces an innovative method that integrates transfer learning with Deep Q-Networks (DQN) for effective financial anomaly identification. The suggested approach boosts detection capabilities by utilising pre-trained models for feature extraction and reinforcement learning for decision-making. The system surpasses conventional methods, attaining 98.7% accuracy, 97.8% F1-score, and 99.1% AUC-ROC on benchmark datasets. In comparison to baseline models like Random Forest and XGBoost, the suggested method shows enhanced accuracy and computing efficiency. These findings confirm the framework's capability for real-time fraud prevention and dynamic risk assessment.

articleTitle: Sustainable Smart Irrigation in Precision Farming using IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The current paper applies computational models based on machine intelligence to enhance the application of water in precision agriculture. This is to establish a reliable tool that can predict the most appropriate ambience of watering, hence enhancing sustainability. It includes what is referred to as sensor integration, and the establishment of a wireless sensor network (WSN). It gives analysis of a well-chosen data log containing essential sensor values like soil moisture, rain, humidity, wind speed and temperature. This paper work elaborates stages of Signal pre-processing, signal conditioning, training and testing performed for available stored dataset. Through the given 105,217 record dataset, smart irrigation accuracy compared using the support vector machine (SVM), random forest, decision tree, artificial neural network as well as other machine learning modes. Database are first trained then evaluated and finally samples are tested. The results of the current study depict that the random forest model is comparatively accurate than the other models with an accuracy of 92.68%. The second best performing method, which is only marginally less accurate than the random forest is decision Trees, with a success rate of 91.83%. SVM and neural network models also gave fairly good performance with accuracy of 90.78 and 90.21 respectively. The random forest model’s accuracy in forecasting ideal irrigation conditions which is further supported by the precision along with F1-Score measures. This paper provides a strong foundation for environmentally friendly water use and offers insightful information about using machine learning techniques for precision agriculture

articleTitle: Advancement in Explainable AI: Bringing Transparency and Interpretability to Machine Learning Models for Use in High-Stakes Decisions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: AI and ML have rapidly altered healthcare, finance, and criminal justice. These models are being used for high-stakes decision-making, raising questions about their openness and interpretability. Explainable AI (XAI), a subfield of machine learning that makes models more intelligible to users, is advancing in key applications where decisions can have a major influence on individuals and society. We begin by discussing black-box models' core issues, which can cause distrust and ethical issues by hiding the decision-making process. We show how model transparency has improved by analysing modern methods including model-agnostic methods, interpretable models, and visualisation tools. LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) can help stakeholders understand how input features affect outcomes. We also emphasise the need of domain expertise in designing successful interpretability methods and user-centric explanations customised to stakeholders' demands. XAI's effects on regulatory compliance, ethical AI practices, and stakeholder confidence are investigated, especially under governance frameworks that require AI accountability and transparency. Finally, we propose developing standardised explainability evaluation metrics, including human factors in interpretability frameworks, and exploring hybrid models that balance accuracy and transparency to bridge the gap between AI advancements and interpretability. This work promotes solutions that empower people to make informed decisions based on trustworthy, interpretable AI systems, contributing to the ethical deployment of AI technologies.

articleTitle: Secure and Transparent Smart Agriculture: Integrating Blockchain Technology with IoT for Enhanced Data Integrity and Efficiency in Agricultural System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: A viable strategy for improving the integrity of information, safety, and operational effectiveness in contemporary agricultural systems is the combination of blockchain-based technology and the Internet of Things. To simplify agricultural operations, this study suggests an accessible and safe architecture that offers end-to-end verification, continuous surveillance, and trustworthy information sharing across participants. The structure guarantees the precision and permanence of information gathered from IoT devices, including sensors that track temperatures, health of crops, moisture levels in the soil, and machinery efficiency, by utilizing the decentralized record of transactions and cryptographic properties of blockchain technology. Information tampering, illegal access, and inaccuracy are frequent problems in agricultural management of information that are reduced by this open method of processing data. Additionally, by enabling computerized processes like condition-based responses and transactional confirmation, smart contracts increase reactivity and decrease the need for manual involvement. Potential advantages of the proposed structure include cost savings, improved trust between agriculturalists, suppliers, and customers, and resource efficiency. Ultimately, this blockchain-IoT connection strengthens the food supply chain security and supports environmentally friendly methods by creating a more robust, based-on-information farming environment.

articleTitle: CryptoQNet: Leveraging Quantum Computing for Enhanced Cryptocurrency Market Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Cryptocurrency markets are characterized by high volatility and nonlinear dynamics, making accurate analysis and forecasting challenging. This study proposes a novel quantum computing-based model, CryptoQNet, to address these challenges by leveraging Quantum Feature Maps, Variational Quantum Circuits, and Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks. CryptoQNet outperforms classical models such as LSTMs and GRUs, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.021 and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.028 for Bitcoin price predictions, compared to 0.038 and 0.045 by LSTMs. For Ethereum, the model achieved an MAE of 0.018 and RMSE of 0.025, demonstrating its robustness in modeling complex market trends. Additionally, CryptoQNet significantly reduced Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) for volatility prediction, achieving 3.2% for Bitcoin and 3.6% for Ethereum, compared to over 5% by classical models. The model also provides enhanced interpretability, identifying price and volume as key factors influencing market trends. While training time is higher due to quantum computations, inference efficiency and accuracy make CryptoQNet a promising tool for financial forecasting. This study highlights the transformative potential of quantum computing in financial market analysis and offers directions for future research in hybrid quantum-classical approaches.

articleTitle: Analyzing Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) Using Passive Honeypot Sensors and Self-Organizing Maps
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of passive honeypot sensors for detecting Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) within IT infrastructures. APTs pose significant risks to government entities, public administrations, and corporations due to their persistent and stealthy nature. The study highlights the commonality of malware propagation as a primary internal attack vector and examines the multivector nature of such attacks, emphasizing their complexity in exploiting various vulnerabilities. The strengths of honeypots, such as low resource requirements and minimal disruption to network traffic, are contrasted with their limitations, including their inability to capture vital network layer threats and the risk of detection by savvy attackers. Furthermore, the use of Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) to classify detected attacks demonstrates how machine learning can aid in visualizing and understanding cyber threats. The findings suggest a need for hybrid security architectures and the incorporation of diverse machine learning techniques to enhance threat detection capabilities, paving the way for future research in the field.

articleTitle: Optimizing Latency and Energy Efficiency in Edge Computing with Reinforcement Learning and TinyML
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Now, a new solution has stepped forward which is promising to offer just that in low latency real time smart networks especially in areas such as Wireless Sensor Networks. This paper puts forward an AI-Driven Adaptive Edge Computing Framework (AEAO) to minimize data processing delay based on real-time resource provisioning and smart task allocation. The framework also initiates lightweight AI models like the TinyML to do inference at certain regions; it also employs RL to manage the resources flexibly. Also, Federated Learning (FL) increases the privacy of the system since models are trained across distributed edge nodes without aggregating sensitive data. The experimental setup of our work assesses the efficacy of the proposed framework in the model healthcare and industrial IoT settings based on the corresponding parameters, including latency, throughput, and energy consumption. Analysis with other methods suggests that delays in processing have decreased, and the accuracy of decisions is higher compared to conventional cloud-oriented and immovable edge computing models. This research captures the possibility of synchronizing computing at the network edge with AI in tackling contemporary challenges of real-time, secure, and efficient data consumption in intelligent networks

articleTitle: Chilli Leaf Disease Prediction System using Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: A vital part of any nation's economy, agriculture provides farmers and their families with the resources they need. Maintaining food security requires the cultivation of chillies, a crucial source of income. When cultivating chillies, a variety of pests and illnesses can result in large losses in yield. Crop illnesses are a serious threat to farmers livelihoods, which emphasizes how critical it is to identify diseases in chilli plants early on at the appropriate stage of growth in order to provide fertilizer on time.The health of the chilli plant is assessed by taking and analyzing a picture of its leaves. A deep learning model called a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture is made to process structured, grid-like data, like pictures. Convolutional, pooling, and fully linked layers are among its several layers. CNNs hierarchical feature extraction capabilities make them extremely effective for tasks like object identification, picture segmentation, and image classification. Using the dataset of chilli leaves, a pretrained deep learning network EfficientNetB0 was used to identify and analyze the diseases (leaf curl, leaf spot, white fly, and yellowish leaf).

articleTitle: Improved Incremental Learning for Classification using Weight Space Rotation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: When incremental learning models encounter new classes, they often experience what is referred to as catastrophic forgetting, wherein previously learned information is lost during the training on new data. This happens for the following reason where deep learning models are expensive to compute and necessitate significant replay of memory, this is very relevant when it involves large datasets, such as those in the case of CIFAR-10. This work introduces a novel method called Weight Space Rotation that aims to improve recall and expedite adaptation in learning new classes by strategically modifying the model's weight space to reduce interference between previously learned and incoming knowledge. WSR does this efficiently without requiring storing earlier examples and is therefore efficient and scalable. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset show that the WSR-enhanced model outperforms conventional techniques in class-incremental learning. WSR achieves this through the allocation of discrete regions in the weight space to different classes, thus enhancing knowledge retention and reducing catastrophic forgetting. This also enhances scalability and reduces computational load as it simplifies regularization processes. The results indicate that WSR significantly enhances the model's capability to learn rapidly new classes in incremental settings while retaining long-term knowledge. For the CIFAR-10 dataset, this approach integrates WSR into the training pipeline of a standard CNN architecture, successfully adapting to new classes while maintaining knowledge of previously learned ones. Experiments confirm that the WSR-enhanced model surpasses current systems by achieving better retention of prior knowledge and faster adaptation to new classes, thereby enhancing performance in class-incremental scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Visibility in Foggy Landmark Images: Advanced Restoration Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The proposed solution to improve the clarity and detail of foggy or hazy images that show historical places, monuments, and archaeological digs an important task for records and preservation. Initially, the effectiveness of two distinct algorithms is explored: Markov Random Fields for image restoration and a Riemannian rank-adaptive method for low-rank matrix completion. Through separate implementations, their individual capabilities in restoring image clarity and detail are evaluated. Afterwards, both algorithms are integrated to synergistically enhance the restoration process. The findings of our proposed solution demonstrate that the combined approach yields significantly improved results, effectively mitigating haze and revealing intricate details obscured in the original images. The integrated methodology offers a promising solution for the restoration and preservation of invaluable cultural heritage imagery. The Combined Restoration approach has the lowest entropy of 6.0 for the enhanced image, indicating a more structured result. It achieves the highest visibility metric of 29.12 and a competitive MSE of 109.93 compared to the hazy image. The proposed system performs best in terms of balancing entropy and visibility enhancement while improving the difference (MSE) between the hazy and restored images.

articleTitle: Video Segmentation and Retrieval Based on Image-Driven Person Recognition for Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The significant increase in the use of surveillance systems for public safety resulted in large volumes of video footage and made manual review inefficient and often impractical. Law enforcement agencies are challenged by the effort to identify suspects or missing persons within hours of video footage. It is also a rather time-consuming and laborious task with a lot of scope for error, which can delay investigations or allow criminals to get away with it. The challenges cited above are why the paper derives an automated video-based people-of-interest identification system using advanced image-driven person recognition techniques. Deep learning models, combining with YOLOv10 for efficient face detection, OpenCV for accurate face recognition and mechanisms for video segmentation and retrieval were used. This system processes video one frame at a time, detecting and matching faces against a predefined target image. At the moment that the system identifies the target person, it also retrieves and stitches together relevant video clips, thus conserving much of the time and effort invested in manual video review. This solution improves the speed and accuracy of person identification in large-scale video data, making it highly valuable for law enforcement and security applications. By automating the video review process, the proposed system enhances operational efficiency, reduces human error, and accelerates the decision-making process, contributing to more effective and timely investigations.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Performance Optimization in Dynamic Routing Protocols for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Improving the energy efficiency of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is crucial for sustainable operation. Therefore, this research explores new concepts of optimized dynamic routing protocols. In careful analysis and empirical comparisons, how could clustering techniques address the WSNs' heterogeneity peculiarities while accounting for energy preservation? This study suggests attractive directions to alleviate energy overheads and prolong the network lifetime, acknowledging the dynamic nature of WSNs. New adaptive techniques are proposed using a hierarchical architecture with the cloop and collective intelligence among sensor nodes. Follow us on Twitter for more updates! With the conventional approaches migrating to Enhanced Energy-Aware Dynamic Sensor routing, a significant enhancement can be observed in static network setups. EEDS outperforms existing schemes and guarantees high packet delivery ratios, low data loss rates, minor end-to-end delays, and greater network throughput. EEDS enables enhanced efficiency due to energy saving and network operations optimization. Upon dynamic network settings, EEDS is a constructive version, further emphasizing the efficiency of WSN operation and address. In this paper, we demonstrate new directions for robust and energy-efficient WSN infrastructure, laying a foundation to propel the operation of IoT applications across India and beyond.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Applications for Real-Time Remote Patient Monitoring and Health Management Through Wearable Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: With smart tech, the Internet of Things (IoT) has become a major force in healthcare, allowing real-time online patient tracking and individual health management. This essay looks at how the Internet of Things can be used in healthcare, focused on how smart tech can be used to collect data and keep an eye on patients all the time. Wearable tech like smartwatches, fitness trackers, and medical-grade gadgets have sensors that keep an eye on things like exercise, heart rate, blood pressure, and carbohydrate levels. When these devices are linked to IoT platforms, they make it easy for healthcare workers to get data, which lets them act quickly and improve patient results. With real-time virtual patient tracking, doctors can keep an eye on their patients' health without having to see them in person as often. This makes care more convenient and cheaper. IoT-enabled gadgets give real-time information about a patient's health, which helps with early discovery of possible health problems, specific treatment plans, and long-term disease management, especially for long-term conditions like diabetes, heart disease, and high blood pressure. Predictive analytics and machine learning algorithms can also be used to look at the data that has been collected and give useful information for proactive care.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning technique where multiple decentralized devices (or servers) collaboratively train a shared model while keeping the training data locally on their machines. Instead of sending the raw data to a central server, each device trains the model locally and only shares the model updates such as model parameters with the central server. This study focuses on the application of FL in the healthcare sector, particularly for predicting cardiovascular disease. Our research explores the performance of various classification algorithms and federated averaging techniques in this setup. The results highlight the potential of FL to provide accurate predictive models while safeguarding patient data in sensitive environments such as hospitals.

articleTitle: Guava Health Monitoring Using Deep Vision: A VGG-16 Model Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: The researchers in this study utilize VGG-16 deep model to classify guava with diseases in three classes - Anthracnose, Fruit Fly, and Healthy Guava. This approach will solve the issues when there are problems with recognition of the diseases affecting a number of crops, resulting in loss to the farmer from economic standpoint. The study used an annotated dataset which was taken under varied natural conditions so that it yields robust results. Over 24 epochs, the model reached a training accuracy of 99.95% and a validation accuracy of 98.86% with high precision of 0.9996, recall of 09996, and area under the curve (AUC) value of 1.0000. The results show that the model is able to extract important features such as dark lesions for Anthracnose, puncture marks for Fruit Fly, and smooth textures for healthy guavas, thus making the classification correct. However, some misclassifications were noted, and these mainly occurred in the Fruit Fly class, thus there is a need for more diversified datasets and pre processing techniques. This study points out the potential that the VGG-16 model may have in fully automating the identification of diseases for guava crops, towards precision agriculture and sustainable farming practices. Future work will include the integration of attention mechanisms and advanced augmentation techniques to enhance the performance of the model and overcome classification challenges.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization in Wireless Sensor Networks using REAMR Protocol for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), optimizing energy consumption, delay and network lifetime is crucial for improving system performance as well as longevity. The paper presents the REAMR (Resource Efficient Adaptive Multi-Route) protocol, a innovative method designed to specify these challenges. Comparative performance investigation were performed against standing protocols, including EELCBRP, LAST, and AFTMR, using performance metrics such as energy consumption, delay as well as network lifetime. The projected REAMR protocol exhibited superior delay reduction, attaining a delay of 1.18 ms at 100th round compared to 1.35ms for EELCBRP, 1.12ms for LAST, and 1.13ms for AFTMR. Correspondingly, in terms of energy effectiveness, REAMR reduced utilization to 510 J at steady-state environments, outperforming EELCBRP, LAST, and AFTMR, which utilized 645 J, 620 J, and 600 J, respectively. Network lifetime investigation further highlighted REAMR's advantages, with a peak lifespan of 320 seconds at the 10th round, outstanding LAST (160 s), AFTMR (265 s), and EELCBRP (100 s). These results show the effectiveness of REAMR in extending network lifespan as well as minimizing resource utilization, making it a promising solution for resource-constrained environments in IoT based applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems Using AI Models and Graph Databases
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This paper outlines the process of generating a Neo4j graph database powered by Language Models (LLMs). The primary goal is to extract structured information from unstructured data, including user profiles, paper briefs, and Slack messages, and convert them into Cypher queries. The data is then ingested into Neo4j to build a graph database that captures relationships between users, paper, technologies, and messages. A pipeline was developed to automate the process, ensuring accurate entity and relationship extraction using predefined templates. This approach allows for efficient data representation and supports consultancy in managing large datasets by generating insightful visualizations and querying capabilities.

articleTitle: Multi-Task Learning Approach for Detecting Multiple Tumors Using CT and MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Smart Computing and Informatics (ESCI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-task learning approach for detection of brain and lung tumors from CT and MRI images. The Inception v3 model, which is a CNN that has an efficient feature extraction process with low computational complexity, was used to classify and locate tumors. The model utilized its multi-scale feature extraction ability to achieve high accuracy and robustness in tumor region differentiation across different datasets. Preprocessing steps such as normalization and data augmentation were found to enhance model generalization, while segmentation techniques improved the accuracy of localizing tumors. Experimental results show that the model was effective, with over 85% accuracy in tumor classification tasks. The proposed system aims to streamline diagnostic workflows, assist radiologists, and enhance healthcare outcomes by providing reliable, automated tumor detection. Future developments include expanding the system to detect additional tumor types and integrating real-time processing capabilities for clinical deployment..
